item.content:encoded:
Teoscar Hernández, Andy Pages hit home runs, Skubal strikes out 10 as Dodgers beat Giants 2-0
Teoscar Hernández and Andy Pages hit home runs in the second inning, leading the Los Angeles Dodgers to a 2-0 win over the San Francisco Giants
SAN FRANCISCO -- Teoscar Hernández and Andy Pages hit home runs in the second inning to back Tarik Skubal's three-hit, seven-inning performance, and the Los Angeles Dodgers beat the San Francisco Giants 2-0 on Friday night.
Shohei Ohtani went 0 for 4 with three strikeouts in his third game back after a 13-game stint on the injured list because of right biceps discomfort.
Skubal (12-7) struck out 10, including four straight during one stretch, and didn't walk a batter in his 10th start for the two-time defending World Series champions since being acquired from Detroit on Aug. 2. The Dodgers had won each of his previous six outings as he went 4-0 over his last four decisions spanning six starts since a loss to Milwaukee on Aug. 16.
It was the two-time reigning AL Cy Young Award winner's fourth double-digit strikeout game of the season, second with Los Angeles.
Roki Sasaki pitched a perfect eighth with a pair of strikeouts before Tanner Scott finished the one hour, 53 minute game for his 24th save. It was the second-fastest game in the ballpark's 27-year history and the fastest Giants-Dodgers game since a 1:50 contest on Aug. 30, 1958, in the second game of a doubleheader, according to MLB.
Giants starter Yunior Marte (0-2) surrendered the two home runs among his six hits in five innings. Earlier in the day, San Francisco welcomed back former closer Camilo Doval, claimed off waivers after they dealt him to the Yankees ahead of the 2025 trade deadline.
Manager Dave Roberts gave utility man Tommy Edman a day off to rest and planned to sit some regulars or give them shorter stints in Sunday's regular-season finale.
Los Angeles has won six straight against the Giants and is 7-4 this year to capture the season series for a fifth straight season, going 47-22 during that time.
The Dodgers have held opponents to four or fewer runs in 108 games, going 82-26 in those contests.
LHP Blake Snell (4-1, 1.86 ERA) pitches Saturday against his former Giants team, which counters with LHP Matt Wilkinson (1-3, 3.65).
___

item.title: [Los Angeles Times] Commentary: Dodgers' three-peat hopes rest on their four aces — and bottom-of-order production
item.dc:creator: Bill Shaikin
item.description: - Click here to listen to this article - - The Dodgers’ path to a third straight World Series title will depend on four frontline starters, but manager Dave Roberts hopes his offense won’t leave them carrying the load. - In a 2-0 win over San Francisco, Teoscar Hernández and Andy Pages offered a timely reminder that the Dodgers will need consistent production from the bottom half of the lineup in the playoffs. - Hernández is a proven October hitter, while Pages is finding his swing after c
item.content:encoded:
- Click here to listen to this article
-
- The Dodgers’ path to a third straight World Series title will depend on four frontline starters, but manager Dave Roberts hopes his offense won’t leave them carrying the load.
- In a 2-0 win over San Francisco, Teoscar Hernández and Andy Pages offered a timely reminder that the Dodgers will need consistent production from the bottom half of the lineup in the playoffs.
- Hernández is a proven October hitter, while Pages is finding his swing after coming back from a broken hand.
SAN FRANCISCO — This is the 60th anniversary of the 1966 World Series, in which the losing team did not score for the final 33 innings of the series.
That losing team was the Dodgers. Over the final three games of the series, Jim Palmer, Wally Bunker and Dave McNally of the Baltimore Orioles each pitched a complete-game shutout.
That art of pitching is not in style today. Yoshinobu Yamamoto pitched two complete games last October, but he cannot pitch every game, even if he left that impression upon the Toronto Blue Jays.
The Dodgers’ clearest and cleanest route to a three-peat nonetheless rests upon the four shoulders of Yamamoto, Tarik Skubal, Blake Snell and Tyler Glasnow. If the four aces can do to October opponents what the 1966 Orioles did to the Dodgers, or some reasonable 21st century facsimile, we’ll see you at the parade.
Does Dodgers manager Dave Roberts believe his starting pitchers will have to carry the load in October?
“I hope not,” Roberts said.
Tarik Skubal gives up just three hits and strikes out 10 in his final start before the postseason to help carry the Dodgers to a 2-0 win over the Giants.
Friday’s 2-0 victory over the San Francisco Giants offered two encouraging swings. Teoscar Hernández and Andy Pages each hit home runs, a reminder that a properly tuned Dodgers offense runs on more than Shohei Ohtani, Mookie Betts, Freddie Freeman and Will Smith.
Skubal scattered three hits and struck out 10 in seven scoreless innings, which would have gone for naught without the Hernández and Pages home runs. Given that the Dodgers were playing the Giants and the remains of their depleted roster, it was something of a warning sign: this could happen against a postseason team.
No team can plan to score a lot of runs against the Dodgers’ starters. The opposing game plan would be to neutralize them and keep the game close enough to where one or two big swings can make the difference. The Giants, who have the National League’s second-worst record, almost pulled it off.
“When you get to the postseason, they’re going to try to eliminate Shohei and try to make other guys beat you,” Roberts said. “So it always sort of comes to the middle to the bottom of the order, where you’ve either got to get guys on base or get hits, get big hits.”
In October, Hernández is who you want at bat. He has homered in six of the seven postseason series he has played for the Dodgers, including each of the last five. In 33 postseason games for the Dodgers, he has driven in 25 runs.
For most players, offensive production drops in October, when batters face the best pitchers from the best teams. For Hernández, his career OPS is .796 in the regular season and .792 in the postseason.
And, for all his summer struggles, he is batting .354 this month, with an OPS just shy of 1.000. He’ll be, as the league-issued hoodies used to say, October ready.
For Pages, however, last October was cruel.
This October was not looking particularly promising, either. Pages missed 27 games because of a broken hand, leaving him the final six games of the regular season to get his swing back into rhythm.
“You think that you take five weeks off,” Roberts said, “that your timing is going to be off a little bit.”
So far, so good: five hits in 12 at-bats, including the home run Friday.
Pages ended the regular season last year with four hits in his final 28 at-bats. That, Roberts said, tells him this October will be different for Pages.
“I think the one thing is the confidence, how he went into last October really scuffling, and it sort of bled into October,” Roberts said, “where I think right now he feels really confident, swinging the bat well, and the hope is that this one bleeds into October as well.
“So, I think it’s definitely a different result going into October, and then also his headspace. There’s a lot more confidence this year.”
In 2025, when the Dodgers won the World Series, they ranked second among the 30 major league clubs in runs scored, and in home runs. In 2024, when they won the World Series, they ranked third in runs scored, and in home runs.
The Dodgers rank fourth in runs scored this year, and seventh in home runs. The offense is down some, if not much. In all the national postseason hype, the Dodgers projections will boil down to one sentence: Can anyone stop those starters?
“I think at first glance that’s what you see in our ballclub,” Roberts said. “But we have a lot of talented, really good hitters and I hope they work hand in hand and not just our pitching and defense carry us.”
For the Dodgers, the postseason opens one week from Saturday. If the Dodgers roll out the 1966 playbook, their October stay will be short.

item.title: [MLB.com] Skubal cruises before Sasaki, Scott prep for postseason roles
item.dc:creator: Sonja Chen
item.description: SAN FRANCISCO -- Tarik Skubal was showing no signs of slowing down in what was shaping up to be his most dominant start as a Dodger. But after throwing seven scoreless innings on 75 pitches, the southpaw was shaking hands and receiving hugs in the visitors' dugout at Oracle Park. item.content:encoded:
SAN FRANCISCO -- Tarik Skubal was showing no signs of slowing down in what was shaping up to be his most dominant start as a Dodger. But after throwing seven scoreless innings on 75 pitches, the southpaw was shaking hands and receiving hugs in the visitors' dugout at Oracle Park.
Skubal struck out 10, gave up just three hits and faced two batters over the minimum in his final regular-season start on Friday night.
His pitch count was in such a good spot that he could have made a bid for the second "Maddux" of his career. But when the bottom of the eighth inning came around, Skubal remained in the dugout and Roki Sasaki relieved him on the mound.
“That was the best we’ve seen," manager Dave Roberts said. "He was on a mission tonight. You could see it. Everything was working. He just went after those guys and did a fantastic job."
While Roberts has maintained that the Dodgers won't approach their final games of the season differently with the No. 2 postseason seed locked in, the 2-0 win over the Giants was an example of how having nothing left to play for changes the calculus of in-game decisions.
With five days off before the NL Division Series begins on Oct. 3 at Dodger Stadium, Roberts isn't necessarily looking to use this weekend for load management. But these final games are the Dodgers' last opportunity to try out players in their postseason roles in a lower-stakes environment.
Had this game taken place a week ago, Skubal may have stayed in to finish off his gem. But the Dodgers had already planned on having Sasaki pitch on Friday, and with only two additional games remaining for him to prepare for his postseason bullpen role, they opted not to deviate from that plan.
Sasaki got his work in, tossing a 1-2-3 eighth inning with two strikeouts in his second appearance back from the injured list. Tanner Scott closed out the victory, the Dodgers' 98th of the season -- which could be a hint at how both leverage arms will be used in the postseason.
"It’s better to have as many guys as you have confidence in in leverage," Roberts said. "So it just allows us to deploy guys whenever we need to."
For much of Skubal's two months as a Dodger, both he and the team maintained that they had not seen him at his best on the mound. Not only was Friday his best performance yet with L.A., but it came against a team that had frustrated him just six days earlier.
Last Saturday, Skubal lasted only five innings while allowing four runs against the Giants at Dodger Stadium. He bemoaned his lack of fastball command, which he believed was the main factor behind the disappointing results.
Skubal didn't just have command of his fastball on Friday. He had command of everything, throwing 60 of his 75 pitches for strikes and going 21-for-23 in first-pitch strikes. He generated 21 whiffs on 43 swings (48.8%), including a season-high 12 on his fastball.
"I think it's the key to who I am. I think it makes me who I am," Skubal said. "I don't know how many pitches I threw tonight, but felt like there were only like 14 or 15 balls out of however many throws. … I'm not going to do that every time, but I think that just speaks to conviction and the pitch-calling."
Said Giants manager Tony Vitello: "He’s going to come right at you, so maybe we could have been a little more aggressive early. But the bottom line is, he was sharper than the other night [in L.A.], and maybe we weren’t as sharp."
While Skubal received minimal run support -- solo homers from Teoscar Hernández and Andy Pages in the second inning -- he had no issues holding the line.
Along with Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Blake Snell and Tyler Glasnow, Skubal is part of the four-man gauntlet the Dodgers will run out in October. In his final tuneup, he looked postseason-ready, and then some.
"Once the months change and the playoffs start, nothing matters," Skubal said. "It's just about winning that game, and that's how I treat every single start. Because I'm just trying to put our team in a position to win a baseball game, and that won't change from today and whenever my next start is."

item.title: [New York Post] Roki Sasaki, Tanner Scott look like Dodgers’ playoff bullpen anchors
item.dc:creator: Dylan Hernandez
item.description: SAN FRANCISCO – The sequence was promising on paper. In practice on Friday night, it was spectacular. Roki Sasaki in the eighth inning. Tanner Scott in the ninth. Manager Dave Roberts emphasized they wouldn’t necessarily be deployed in that order come the playoffs, but their performances in the Dodgers’ 2-0 victory over the Giants indicated they could be the foundation of a championship-caliber bullpen for the Dodgers. “I don’t want you to pigeonhole me into using these guys in certain roles, bu
item.content:encoded:
SAN FRANCISCO – The sequence was promising on paper. In practice on Friday night, it was spectacular.
Roki Sasaki in the eighth inning.
Tanner Scott in the ninth.
Manager Dave Roberts emphasized they wouldn’t necessarily be deployed in that order come the playoffs, but their performances in the Dodgers’ 2-0 victory over the Giants indicated they could be the foundation of a championship-caliber bullpen for the Dodgers.
“I don’t want you to pigeonhole me into using these guys in certain roles, but, yeah, I think it’s just better to have as many guys that you have confidence in leverage (situations),” Roberts said.
Sasaki followed a seven-inning effort by starter Tarik Skubal by striking out two batters in a perfect eighth inning.
Scott retired the side in the ninth to record his 24th save.
On their World Series run last year, the bullpen was something the Dodgers had to work around. They were extremely dependent on their starting pitchers, whom they counted on not only to pitch deeper into games but also make relief contributions. Sasaki’s emergence as closer was as much a reflection of their lack of options as it was of the Japanese fireballer’s gifts.
The Dodgers should enter the playoffs next month with an entirely different feel.
Scott has recovered from his nightmare season last year, looking more like the Padres relief ace who shut down Shohei Ohtani in the 2024 playoffs to earn a $72-million payday with the Dodgers.
As for the 24-year-old Sasaki, he looks even better as a reliever than he did last year.
“I think the fastball’s better,” Roberts said. “I think the split’s better. It’s also nice that he’s already done it. So, just in total, he’s just a better pitcher than he was last year and a lot more confident. And certainly, the stuff was really good the last couple outings.”
Four of the six fastballs Sasaki threw were clocked at faster than 100 mph.
The other two registered readings of more than 99 mph.
“Overall, he just keeps getting better,” Scott said. “Even when he was starting, I thought he was pretty dominant. For him to get moved to the bullpen as we go into October, it’s huge for us.”
Sasaki started seven games after the All-Star break and was 2-0 with a 3.05 earned-run average. A blister on his pitching hand landed him on the injured list. When he returned earlier this week, he did so as a reliever.
He also struck out two batters in his other relief appearance, a scoreless inning on Tuesday against the San Diego Padres.
“Throughout the season, I’ve sharpened myself technically,” Sasaki said in Japanese. “Compared to last year, I feel much better in that respect.”
Sasaki will likely pitch next in the regular-season finale on Sunday, Roberts said.
He could close out games again in October, as Roberts said there could be games in which he calls on Scott to pitch against a particularly dangerous segment of the opposing lineup earlier in the game.
Scott said he was open to pitching in any situation.
“Just get outs,” Scott said. “That’s all that matters in October. Get outs.
“October is about winning every single game. It really doesn’t matter what roles you get asked to do. Just go out there and do it.”

item.dc:creator: Nelson Espinal

item.content:encoded:
Los Angeles Dodgers pitcher Roki Sasaki delivered another impressive relief outing against the San Francisco Giants in his new role.
Sasaki the dominant reliever
Roki Sasaki pitched a clean inning on Friday, September 25th, recording two strikeouts and allowing no hits or walks.
Sasaki needed just 14 pitches to get through the order. His pitches all came in at a higher velocity than his season average.
His fastball stood out, averaging 100 mph, 2.2 mph above his season average; his splitter was 1.7 mph up, and his slider was 0.4 mph up as well, according to Baseball Savant.
He got two whiffs and three called strikes. More importantly, the horizontal break on all of his pitches was higher than average, and his slider got some extra vertical induced.
This was only Sasaki’s second outing in 2026 as a reliever, a role he has assumed since returning from the injured list after a blister on his middle finger.
His first outing was on Tuesday, September 22nd, when Sasaki allowed two hits but stranded both baserunners with two strikeouts.
Dave Roberts is impressed with Sasaki
After Friday’s game, manager Dave Roberts noted how dominant Sasaki is pitching in his new role.
“I think the fastball is better. I think the split’s better. And it’s also nice that he’s already done it,” Roberts said.
“Just in total, he’s just a better pitcher than he was last year and a lot more confident. And certainly the stuff was really good the last couple of outings.”
As a right-handed arm, Sasaki has established himself as a trustworthy arm, whether in the bullpen or the starting rotation.
He was the postseason closer last year, but with the rise of Tanner Scott and Edgardo Henriquez, along with the surprise emergence of Edwin Diaz, Sasaki will not be relied on as much as the bullpen trust tree grows.
“I think it’s just better to have as many guys that you have confidence in and leverage. It just allows us to deploy guys whenever we need to. I feel comfortable with a lot of guys at the back end for sure,” Roberts added.
Whether he comes in during the seventh, eighth, or ninth inning, Sasaki is no longer a question mark, and he pitches like an exclamation point.

item.content:encoded:
El campocorto de los Dodgers de Los Ángeles, Mookie Betts, está teniendo un septiembre demente en el plato y parece alguno que puede sobrellevar la ataque en la postemporada.
El demente septiembre de Betts
Betts está bateando .367 en septiembre hasta el viernes, con 21 carreras impulsadas, seis jonrones y nueve dobles.
Tiene un OPS de 1.117 y un wRC+ de 219, ambas métricas resaltan cuán elitista ha sido. Ha sido, con diferencia, su mejor mes de la temporada y es similar a sus mejores marcas como MVP.
Anuncio
Da boletos el 16% de sus apariciones en el plato y se poncha sólo el 8,5% de las veces.
Su enfoque en el plato luce excelente, con buenas decisiones de swing y un esforzado dominio de la zona de strike que empuja a los lanzadores a realizar lanzamientos más desafiantes de los que desearían.
Cuando hace swing, tiene 32 bolas aceptablemente golpeadas este mes y la velocidad de salida promedio es de 92.6 mph, la más entrada del año hasta el momento.
Por qué los Dodgers necesitaban esta producción de Betts
Para sorpresa de nadie, Betts fue el mejor bateador del equipo en septiembre. Su wRC+ solo rivaliza con Josue De Paula, aunque el tamaño de su muestra fue mucho más pequeño que el de Betts.
Anuncio
Shohei Ohtani se perdió la viejo parte del mes por una ultraje en el padrino derecho, mientras que Andy Pages asimismo se perdió la viejo parte del mes y regresó solo en los últimos días.
Por otra parte, Freddie Freeman y Tommy Edman se han vuelto prácticamente fríos, lo que solo aumenta aún más la escazes de que alguno dé un paso al frente.
Betts ha sido el hombre que ha llevado la ataque, con 25 carreras ponderadas creadas, según FanGraphs, la viejo cantidad en el equipo, superado por Teoscar Hernández, quien tiene 19.
Con su surgimiento y la caída de Edman, Betts asumió el puesto de primer bate hasta que Ohtani regresó, y su maniobra ha sido tan bueno que incluso luego del regreso de la superestrella japonesa, el manager Dave Roberts todavía mantiene a Betts como líder contra los zurdos.
Anuncio
¿Podrá Betts sustentar esto en la postemporada?
Betts tiene un historial de mejorar durante los playoffs. En su primera temporada con los Dodgers, bateó .296/.378/.493 con OPS+ de 135 hasta octubre, cuando los Dodgers ganaron la Serie Mundial.
2021 fue más de lo mismo, bateando .319/.377/.404 con 116 wRC+. 2022 y 2023 terminaron temprano para los Dodgers y Betts tuvo problemas entreambos primaveras.
En 2024, cuando los Dodgers ganaron uno de sus primeros títulos consecutivos, Betts estuvo mágico, bateando .290/.387/.585 con 151 wRC+.
Durante la viejo parte de la temporada, Betts no fue lo que los fanáticos de Mookie esperaban, con un bautizo promedio de la muérdago y una gran defensa en el campocorto.
Anuncio
A partir de mediados de agosto y hasta septiembre, cambió el estandarte y dejó al manager Dave Roberts impresionado y sorprendido.
“No podría decirte que vi esto [coming]”, dijo Roberts. “Pero se ha vuelto más esforzado. Ha trabajado duro en eso… Y el hecho de que todo salga aceptablemente ha sido increíble. Simplemente no importa dónde lo golpees, a quién se enfrenta, [what’s] la situación… está tomando buenos turnos al bate”.
Betts, mientras tanto, sabía que su antigua producción a nivel de Tahúr Más Valioso todavía estaba en él.
“Sé que todavía soy capaz de hacerlo”, dijo Betts. “Sé que estaba ahí en alguna parte”.
De cara a octubre, pocos bateadores deberían hacer apreciar mejor a los fanáticos.
Su experiencia, anejo con su nueva producción, deberían ayudarlo a encajar en la fórmula, anejo con el pitcheo abridor de calidad, que lo colocará a él y a los Dodgers de 2026 en la inmortalidad de la MLB.

item.title: [Dodgers Nation] Mookie Betts' Monster September Is Setting Up a Dodgers October
item.dc:creator: Nelson Espinal

He is walking 16% of plate appearances and striking
item.content:encoded:
Los Angeles Dodgers shortstop Mookie Betts is having a crazy September at the plate, and he looks like someone who can carry the offense in the postseason.
Betts’ Crazy September
Betts is hitting .367 in September entering Friday, with 21 RBIs, six home runs, and nine doubles.
He has a 1.117 OPS and a 219 wRC+, both metrics highlighting just how elite he has been. It has been his best month of the season by far, and it is akin to his MVP bests.
He is walking 16% of plate appearances and striking out on just 8.5% of the time.
His approach at the plate looks great, with good swing decisions and a strong command of the strike zone that pushes pitchers to throw more challenging pitches than they would want.
When he does swing, he has 32 hard-hit balls this month, and the average exit velocity is 92.6 mph, the highest of the year thus far.
Why the Dodgers needed this production from Betts
To no one’s surprise, Betts was the team’s best hitter in September. His wRC+ is only rivaled by Josue De Paula, though his sample size was much smaller than Betts’.
Shohei Ohtani missed most of the month with a right-arm injury, while Andy Pages also missed the majority of the month, returning only in the last few days.
Additionally, Freddie Freeman and Tommy Edman have gone mostly cold, only further increasing the need for someone to step up.
Betts has been the guy to carry the offense, with 25 weighted runs created, according to FanGraphs, the most on the team, second to Teoscar Hernandez, who has 19.
With his emergence and Edman’s slump, Betts took over the leadoff spot until Ohtani returned, and his play has been so good that even after the Japanese superstar returned, manager Dave Roberts still has Betts lead off against lefties.
Can Betts keep this up in the postseason?
Betts has a track record of stepping up during the playoffs. In his first season with the Dodgers, he hit .296/.378/.493 with a 135 OPS+ through October, when the Dodgers won the World Series.
2021 was more of the same, hitting .319/.377/.404 with a 116 wRC+. 2022 and 2023 ended early for the Dodgers, and Betts struggled both years.
In 2024, when the Dodgers won one of their first consecutive titles, Betts was magical, hitting .290/.387/.585 with a 151 wRC+.
For most of the season, Betts wasn’t the Mookie fans expected, with league-average hitting and great defense at shortstop.
Starting in mid-August and into September, he flipped the script and left manager Dave Roberts impressed and surprised.
“I couldn’t tell you that I saw this [coming],” Roberts said. “But he’s got stronger. He’s worked hard on that … And just for it to come together has been great. It just doesn’t matter where you hit him, who he’s facing, [what’s] the situation –– he’s taking good at-bats.”
Betts, meanwhile, knew his former MVP-level production was still in him.
“I know I’m still capable of it,” Betts said. “I know it was in there somewhere.”
Heading into October, few hitters should make fans feel better.
His experience, along with his newfound production, should help him fit into the formula, alongside the quality starting pitching, that puts him and the 2026 Dodgers into MLB immortality.

item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers have their sights set on winning a third consecutive World Series, which would make them the first team since the New York Yankees, over a quarter century ago, to achieve that feat.
The Dodgers, who are about to open up a series against the rival San Francisco Guardians on the cusp of the MLB postseason, have welcomed back catcher Dalton Rushing off the injured list, but also had to make a corresponding move to open up room on the roster.
The Los Angeles Dodgers Have Optioned Alex Freeland To The Minors
In a corresponding move, the Dodgers have optioned Alex Freeland to the minors, opening up a spot for Rushing.
“The Dodgers have reinstated catcher Dalton Rushing from the injured list and optioned IF Alex Freeland,” the Dodgers reported on X, formerly known as Twitter.
However, the move wasn’t fully well received by fans.
“All Rushing can do is pinch hit. Which means you burn the guy he hits for, Rushing, and a replacement fielder the next inning. Peak Dave Roberts thinking,” one fan noted.
This fan said, “Meaningless series vs. the Giants and could’ve been testing out De Paula in left field this weekend but Alex Call has compromising photos of Friedman apparently.”
This fan said, “Rushing’s elbow is completely fried and this is the second time they’ve recalled him from the IL. I honestly don’t understand it at all.”
Alex Freeland Has Been Optioned To Triple-A By The Dodgers
Freeland was taken by the Dodgers the third round of the 2022 MLB Draft. He began his professional career with Rancho Cucamonga, hitting .313 in eight games, before spending 2023 with Great Lakes, where he batted .240 with nine home runs and 57 RBI.
Freeland climbed through three levels in 2024, finishing the season with Triple-A Oklahoma City. Across 136 games, he hit .260 with 18 homers, 74 RBI and 31 stolen bases.
He started 2025 with Oklahoma City before receiving his first MLB promotion in late July. Freeland debuted for Los Angeles on July 30, collecting his first hit against Cincinnati, and hit his first major-league homer off Yu Darvish on Aug. 22. He hit .190 with two home runs and six RBI in 29 games with the Dodgers, while posting a .263/.384/.451 line with 16 homers and 82 RBI in 106 Triple-A games.
Freeland made the Dodgers’ 2026 Opening Day roster and began the season splitting time at second base with Miguel Rojas.
Freeland has appeared in 89 games so far this season for the Dodgers, and has four home runs with 21 RBI along with a .234 batting average and a .652 OPS.

item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers activated Dalton Rushing off the 10-day injured list and optioned Alex Freeland to Triple-A Oklahoma City prior to Friday’s game against the San Francisco Giants.
Freeland heads back to the Minors after joining the Dodgers when active rosters expanded on Sept. 1. He was chosen over an outfield prospect despite Teoscar Hernández and Kyle Tucker both struggling at the time. James Tibbs III at one point appeared to be the expected choice for the Dodgers’ extra position player.
Instead the team elected for Freeland, who hit .250/.413/.389 with two doubles, one home run and two RBI over 17 games (10 starts) this month. Freeland last played on Saturday against the San Francisco Giants.
Freeland endured an inconsistent year after making the Dodgers’ Opening Day roster over Hyeseong Kim. He had some stretches of promise not only at the Major League level, but while with the Comets as well. The 25-year-old conceivably will join Oklahoma City for their Triple-A National Championship game in Las Vegas on Saturday.
With Freeland getting optioned this late in the season, he is not a candidate to make the Dodgers’ postseason roster for the National League Division Series. He would not be eligible to get added in time for Game 1 on Saturday, Oct. 3, unless taking the spot of an injured player.
Rushing is back from a second stint on the injured list due to trouble with his right elbow. The first instance was due to a slight tear in the UCL, but the latest came because of a flexor tendon problem.
It prompted the Dodgers to halt Rushing’s throwing progression and he now has three games to seemingly make up for lost time. Rushing had been projected to be the left-handed bat off the bench for the postseason, but Josue De Paula may now have the inside track for that role.
Dodgers manager Dave Roberts indicated Rushing would receive a maximum of three at-bats as a pinch-hitter this weekend.
Like Andy Pages and Shohei Ohtani earlier this week, Rushing is back without having gone on a rehab assignment in part because of the Minor League season ending. Though, he did log at-bats against Will Klein, who likewise is hopeful to earn a role with the Dodgers come October.

item.title: [Sports Illustrated] Dodgers Demote Infielder, Officially Activate Dalton Rushing Before Giants Series

item.description: The Los Angeles Dodgers made a roster move ahead of Friday's series opener against the San Francisco Giants, activating catcher Dalton Rushing off the injured list. However, the Dodgers wanted to give him an opportunity to get a couple pinch-hit at-bats over the season's final three game
item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers made a roster move ahead of Friday's series opener against the San Francisco Giants, activating catcher Dalton Rushing off the injured list.
In order to make room on the active roster, infielder Alex Freeland was optioned.
Rushing is continuing to recover from a torn UCL in his elbow and will be unable to play defense for the remainder of the season. However, the Dodgers wanted to give him an opportunity to get a couple pinch-hit at-bats over the season's final three games as an audition for his potential role in the postseason.
“At the most it would be three pinch-hit at-bats, so just conduct at-bats and see what you got,” Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said of the plan for Rushing. “Just the circumstances of his situation, it’s just tough to just be hurt, come back, then be hurt again, and then take three pinch-hit at-bats to potentially then say, ‘Hey, you’re on the roster.’
“What he’s done for us this season certainly deserves some [playoff] consideration. That’s kind of giving him the respect and thoughtfulness of what he’s done for us.”
Rushing has appeared in 78 games this season, hitting .249 with 12 home runs, 36 RBIs and an OPS of .798. After starting once or twice a week, he took over the full-time duties following Will Smith's neck injury.
However, Rushing then suffered an elbow flare-up, causing the Dodgers to reshape their catching tandem at the trade deadline.
Rushing was able to return on Sept. 1, but suffered a setback while attempting to progress in his throwing program. He was placed back on the IL on Sept. 6, and has been out ever since.
“In my eyes, me trying to throw is me showing them that obviously I want to help the team win,” Rushing said to the LA Times. “I want to give us the best available option that we have at that moment, and that was my whole plan all along. So I hope they see there wasn’t any selfishness in that.”
Rushing understands he's in a difficult spot to earn a spot on the postseason roster, especially with the emergence of the left-handed hitting Josue De Paula. However, he's hoping to prove over the final three days of the regular season that he can be an asset come October.
“The at-bat’s really are the only side that I can truly help them in,” Rushing said. “Even then, it’s just a pinch-hit opportunity and no defense included, so I know that ties their hands up a little bit. But yeah, I’m excited.”
“No hard feelings on either end,” he added. “Obviously you want to play baseball. You feel healthy again to an extent. You feel healthy swinging a bat, so yeah, I want to get back soon.”
Dodgers Option Alex Freeland
As for Freeland, he's officially not an option for the NLDS roster, barring an injury. Across 89 games this season, he hit .234 with an OPS of .652.

As a corresponding move, the team decided to option top prospect Josue De Paula. However, the Dodgers optioning De Paula was always going to be the move, as they wanted him to continue getting o
item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers are finally getting healthy just in time for the postseason as they activated superstar Shohei Ohtani off the injured list this week.
As a corresponding move, the team decided to option top prospect Josue De Paula.
De Paula made a name for himself in 11 contests for Los Angeles, and many fans hoped the Dodgers would go another route when they activated Ohtani.
However, the Dodgers optioning De Paula was always going to be the move, as they wanted him to continue getting opportunities to play at Triple-A before potentially being an option in the postseason.
Manager Dave Roberts loved what he saw from the 21-year-old, and revealed the message he gave De Paula when informing him about his demotion to Triple-A.
“This was the original thought, that once Shohei gets back, we’re going to send him out,” Roberts said. “We had a runway to give him, which we gave him and he performed more than admirably. This also, as far as the timing, just gives us an opportunity to potentially have him back for the postseason. He’s a part of the conversation, and he’searned that, and that’s what I told him last night.”
He added: "It was actually an easier conversation than you guys probably would expect, given how well he’s performed."
Josue De Paula Has Made a Strong Case for the Postseason
De Paula was fantastic in his first 11 games in the majors. He recorded a .323 batting average with a 1.081 OPS, one home run, seven RBIs and 10 hits in 31 at-bats.
De Paula only struck out five times and drew 11 walks.
De Paula's maturity at the plate was evident before his major league debut, and he showed exactly why once he stepped into the batter's box.
His advanced plate discipline and impressive strike-zone judgment are exactly why he is a candidate to make the postseason roster.
“He's done everything he can to put himself in a position to be in the conversation for us as we're making our postseason roster,” president of baseball operations Andrew Friedman said.
One area De Paula does need to improve on is his defense. That won't come to fruition until the offseason, though.
"I just think that — just being candid — I don’t think that he’s valued it as much as he will," Roberts said recently. "And it just has to be important. Certainly, when you get to the big leagues, outs are important, converting outs are important."
The Dodgers have 12 players who appear to be locks to make the postseason roster. De Paula has certainly made his case to be the 13th position player in October, but he'll be competing with Dalton Rushing, who's set to be activated on Friday.

item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers have been without Edgardo Henriquez for nearly two weeks, but things are trending toward the right-hander returning in time for the postseason.
Henriquez landed on the 15-day injured list on Sept. 14 due to low back discomfort. An MRI a few days later ruled out an oblique injury and showed a low-grade back strain, which was a positive outcome, especially given how late in the season it was.
Henriquez hoped he would be able to return for the National League Division Series, and now his optimism for that is growing with each day.
The 24-year-old threw a bullpen session after his symptoms improved, and he believes he’ll be ready for the playoffs, according to Fabian Ardaya of The Athletic.
Edgardo Henriquez said he threw a bullpen session yesterday, his first since landing on the IL. His back is in a better spot after dealing with some discomfort for about a month.
He said he thinks he can be ready for the NLDS.
The Dodgers have also said they expect Henriquez to return for the playoffs as he goes through his throwing program. “So as I understand it from before, we still expect him to be back for the postseason,” manager Dave Roberts said.
The Dodgers only have three remaining games, so Henriquez’s regular season has already ended. But with the Dodgers clinching the second seed in the NL, they won’t play their first postseason game until Saturday, Oct. 3.
That gives Henriquez extra time to fully recover and continue building back up.
When he returns, the Dodgers pitching staff will be at its healthiest in recent memory and in a better position than the previous two years when they won back-to-back World Series titles.
Edgardo Henriquez’s 2026 season
During Henriquez’s final outing of his 2026 regular season, he allowed two runs against the Miami Marlins. He retired just two batters after entering in the eighth inning, trying to protect a 3-0 lead.
Despite ending on a poor note, the flamethrower finished his 2026 season with 61 appearances in a breakout year. Henriquez went 4-1 with a 2.85 ERA and also set a Dodgers record for the fastest pitch thrown on a strikeout earlier this year.
Roberts said Henriquez could receive more save opportunities before he landed on the IL. It’s unlikely the Dodgers throw him right into a save chance when he returns, but Henriquez should still see plenty of high-leverage work upon his return.

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Eric Lauer and other recent Dodgers regular-season helpers
item.dc:creator: Estevão Maximo
item.description: The success of a dominant team over a lengthy period like the Dodgers' relies on an adaptability to work your way through multiple iterations of a roster. While in the postseason you can find success in different ways, one aspect of regular-season success is how you handle injuries, particularly for a team as cautious as the Dodgers. A common theme in recent seasons has been the Dodgers' pitching staff overcoming all sorts of obstacles to consistently provide terrific numbers. Postseason basebal
item.content:encoded:
The success of a dominant team over a lengthy period like the Dodgers' relies on an adaptability to work your way through multiple iterations of a roster. While in the postseason you can find success in different ways, one aspect of regular-season success is how you handle injuries, particularly for a team as cautious as the Dodgers.
A common theme in recent seasons has been the Dodgers' pitching staff overcoming all sorts of obstacles to consistently provide terrific numbers. Postseason baseball funnels everything, and meritocracy only takes you so far when the goal is to win short series, but that doesn't mean the impact of productive but unceremoniously overlooked starters shouldn't get the credit it rightfully deserves.
There are layers of this tier, and we're not here to discuss the Justin Wrobleskis of the world, who'll morph into a different but still impactful role because their talent level demands a presence on the postseason roster, one way or another. This is an article for the Eric Lauers — pitchers who served a very specific and much-needed purpose in the regular season, but whose eventual playoff showing would only come in garbage-time scenarios; in Lauer's case, not even that, given he has ended the season on the injured list.
When Blake Snell and Tyler Glasnow went down this year, as they often do in the regular season, the Dodgers took to the market early in the season for a veteran steady presence. Lauer did more than just go out there with league-average production or so.
The former Brewer worked on some adjustments with the Dodgers' pitching staff and led the team to a win in each of his first nine starts, boasting an ERA under 3.00 through that period. It'd be no stretch to argue that, at the very least, this chase for a playoff bye would look a lot different with a ton more pressure had it not been for Lauer's timely production. His final line with the Dodgers looks far worse than he pitched due to a couple of blowups against NL Central teams (4.50 ERA in 12 games), but his impact through most of that period was undeniable.
Even in the best of moments for Lauer with the Dodgers prior to his season-ending injury, it was evident that he would not play a key role in the playoffs, but it was about doing a specific job. While he was the best example in this year's current squad, going back through the recent track record, the names pile up, and here we'll look at a few others that might stand out—who perhaps didn't receive the right amount of due at the time, and certainly not when playoff ball rolled around.
Prospects with potentially limited big-league upside
This season's starting pitching problems are a cakewalk in comparison with what this team had to deal with a year ago. On the lookout for starting pitching contributions for much of the 2025 campaign, the Dodgers saw Dustin May come full circle on a sped-up version of your traditional career, entering the innings-eater portion far earlier than anyone would've anticipated, one of three starters on the team to cover 100-plus innings, this despite getting dealt at the deadline.
May, more than probably any other pitcher on this list, really pushed the envelope of what we can consider helpful volume, even with the caveat of potential uncertainty on door number two. It's easy to be dismissive of his ERA in the high 4.00s that got progressively worse until the team dealt him when it got healthier in the second half—through the majority of those innings, though, it literally had no one else. And if we want to get a little cute about it, the health he displayed in that period certainly played a role in helping the Dodgers land the offer they sought, with James Tibbs III joining the fold. It's about finding advantages anywhere.
If May represents the low end of the expectation pool for a pitcher of his caliber receiving this type of role in a contending team, a year prior Gavin Stone showed the best-case scenario. On the way to their second World Series of this era, it was the youngster Stone who led the Dodgers in innings pitched that regular season, before injuries cut short his campaign and development, which has been affected until the present day.
Even before the injuries, it was becoming increasingly clear in the second half of that 2024 campaign that Stone's postseason role would diminish, particularly so after the Dodgers acquired Jack Flaherty at the deadline. The changeup-heavy approach with below-average strikeout numbers caused enough concern that he likely wouldn't have stuck in the rotation one way or another.
Both in very different places right now, one still in the organization, May and Stone were once regarded as highly touted pitching prospects. Although their development wasn't as smooth as the Dodgers would've liked, they showed up to provide support at times of need, and their contributions meant a lot in championship-winning seasons.
Former stars in unique spots
Clayton Kershaw gave his best years to the Dodgers when they weren't nearly at their best and did so with the utmost grace and power. After a second chapter of his career, still dominant but maybe not quite Kershaw-dominant, came to an end in 2023, he stuck around for a couple of more years and only then genuinely looked mortal, but still quite helpful.
Missing the bulk of the 2024 season recovering from shoulder surgery, Kershaw came back healthier for one final year in 2025, and while his All-Star nomination might've been a tad sentimental, the 11-2 record was eye-catching, with a productive 124 ERA+.
Sitting below 90 MPH on his heater, there were clear limitations to what Kershaw could provide, but not only did he appear on the postseason roster. But he also managed to get one immense out in the never-ending Game 3 of that year's World Series. The plan was never to have him play a big role in October, but circumstances gave him a memorable cameo.
Going back to the regular season contributions, Kershaw, alongside May, was one of three Dodgers starters to surpass 100 innings in 2025. On the subject of his impact on that 93-69 record, there was nothing sentimental about it; he thoroughly helped a team that relied on him far more than expected.
Going back a few more years, the Dodgers needed to take on the David Price contract in order for the Mookie Betts deal to go through with Boston. And although that was a bad deal, it didn't mean Price couldn't be of assistance.
Opting out of the 2020 campaign, Price came in 2021 ready to embrace whatever role the Dodgers had for him, and he delivered a 105 ERA+ in over 70 innings, moving back and forth between the rotation and the bullpen. While the rotation was healthier that year, it didn't mean his presence went unnoticed, one of the more heavily used arms navigating between the rotation and the bullpen.
The OGs of this role in this run
When you first started reading this article, there is a decent chance one of the first names that came to mind was Mitch White or, particularly, Ross Stripling — the latter personally thanked by Dave Roberts in the World Series-winning speech back in 2020, a year in which he was traded from the team that August.
Between 2016 and 2019, Stripling pitched nearly 400 innings of regular-season baseball with a 115 ERA+, moving around to whatever role fit the team best. Seeing them finally break through to win it all the year in which he was dealt (2020) quickly made Dave and many others remember all he had done for this team.
It's a shame that at his best in 2018, working primarily as a starter, Stripling saw his campaign cut short due to injury and couldn't be available in that postseason. In 2020, the Dodgers stuck with him as much as possible, but eventually cutting ties seemed like the only answer with an ERA well above 5.00 in a shortened campaign.
White is the ideal example to note how, in most of these cases, whether the Dodgers get these players late, early, or even develop them from the minors, they seem to shine brightest here. In three seasons with the Dodgers, White had a 116 ERA+ in a little over 100 innings. Not only did he fail to reach similar heights after leaving the team, but his exposure was very limited, covering just 79.1 innings in two seasons since. Out of the bigs since 2024.
Surely there were other names in recent memory that we might've skipped over. Let us know who your favorite regular-season starting pitcher contributor is, or even all-time. It's always a fun conversation to have with no right or wrong answer.

item.content:encoded:
Los Angeles Dodgers manager Dave Roberts had some high praise for right-handed pitcher Emmet Sheehan after his last start, hinting at the strong possibility of him making the team's postseason roster.
Sheehan, who was recently optioned back to Triple-A Oklahoma City, seems like a lock to join the team for the National League Division Series next weekend.
“I’ve loved the version we’ve seen of Emmet the last three outings,” Roberts said. “He’s been fantastic.
“We’ve seen confidence. We’ve seen when you’re essentially fighting for your life to create an opportunity for yourself. That’s what I see. There’s urgency. I like the way that he’s trusting his stuff. He’s in a good spot physically, and you know the performance has been fantastic.”
The 26-year-old pitcher was masterful in his final outing of the regular season on Sunday in the Dodgers' win over the San Francisco Giants, pitching 5.1 shutout innings and striking out nine batters. He entered in the second inning after Jack Dreyer pitched the first, giving him more experience coming out of the bullpen.
Overall, Sheehan has looked incredible in his three September outings. He's allowed just one run over 17 innings with 24 strikeouts.
“I think that obviously there’s a 97 [mph] that plays better, but 94-95 commanded still misses bats,” Roberts said of Sheehan. “That’s one part of it. The other part of it is holding the velocity. And so, for me, the last three or four since he’s been back here, he’s held those 94s and 95s for the, call it, 85 pitches.”
This season, Sheehan owns a 5-8 record with a 4.57 ERA, 1.18 WHIP and 132 strikeouts in 112.1 innings across 23 appearances.
Sheehan is expected to be in the Dodgers' bullpen for this year's postseason, just as he was last year.
During the 2025 postseason, Sheehan made six relief appearances, posting an 8.59 ERA and recording six strikeouts over 7.1 innings. However, he said he's more prepared this time around, and expects to have better results in his now more familiar role.
“Definitely,” Sheehan said. “I think the routine of everything can be a little bit hard to adjust to right away. So having that experience helps a lot. Just getting back into that, I know what I need to do to get ready to go into the game.”
Sheehan will give the Dodgers a multi-inning option out of the bullpen. If he's pitching like he has over the last few weeks, he could be a serious weapon for LA.

With the Los Angeles Dodgers preparing for the upcoming 2026 MLB Playoffs, the team is looking to get back key players from injuries, with catcher Dalton Rushing about to return to the roster. As the Dodgers look to finalize their playoff strategy ahead of the postseason, the team gets huge news regarding the 25-year-old catcher.
According to MLB.com, Rushing is "set to be activated" from the 10-day injured list for the final regular-season series against the San Francisco Giants. Rushing last played for Los Angeles Sept. 4, as the star had been dealing with "right elbow discomfort," though it goes beyond that, as he'll only be a hitter this season after a "partial tear of the ulnar collateral ligament in his right elbow.
Rushing will have three games to prove his worth on the Dodgers' postseason roster, but there's no denying that Los Angeles manager Dave Roberts wants to give him a shot.

"Just the circumstances of his situation, it's just tough to just be hurt, be back, then be hurt again," Roberts said Thursday, via Sonja Chen of MLB.com. "And then take three pinch-hit at-bats, potentially, and then say, 'Hey, you're on the roster.' What he's done for us this season certainly deserves some consideration. That's kind of giving him the respect and thoughtfulness of what he's done for us."
More on the decision regarding Dodgers' Dalton Rushing
With three games left in the regular season for the Dodgers, Rushing has recorded a .249 batting average to go along with 12 home runs and 36 RBIs in 78 games and 221 plate appearances. While the small sample size of three games could be discouraging for his chances at making Los Angeles' playoff roster, Dodgers president of baseball operations Andrew Friedman is also looking at his season as a whole.
"He's done everything he can to put himself in a position to be in the conversation for us as we're making our postseason roster," Friedman said.
At any rate, it remains to be seen how Rushing plays after returning from the injured list with an elbow issue as Friday starts the series against the Giants.

item.content:encoded:
Los Angeles Dodgers fans have spoken, and they want rookie Josue De Paula back with the team to provide a spark.
Why the Dodgers Demoted De Paula
After 11 stellar games, in which De Paula looked amazing at the plate, the Dodgers demoted him on Wednesday, September 23rd, sending him back to the minors.
With Shohei Ohtani returning from the injured list, he would assume the designated hitter role from De Paula. Additionally, Dalton Rushing is returning to get some at-bats and make his case for a postseason roster spot.
De Paula was hitting .323/.500/.545 with a 1.081 OPS, making pitchers work and bringing a youthful edge to an older roster.
After his demotion, manager Dave Roberts and president of baseball operations Andrew Friedman both praised De Paula and made it clear he will be considered for a spot on the postseason roster.
Since he was demoted on Wednesday and players must wait 10 days to be promoted back to the major leagues, he would be in line to return in time for Game 1 of the NLDS.
While the decision-makers are giving Rushing a chance to make his case and weigh their options, Dodgers Nation has already decided.
Dodgers Fans Demand De Paula
Following his demotion, the Dodgers have scored just two runs over the last 18 innings, losing both games to the San Diego Padres.
In his last game on Tuesday, September 22nd, De Paula went 2-for-3 with a triple, a walk, and a stolen base.
With the two-game cold stretch since his absence, fans want him back in the mix.
“Hmm, maybe sending JDP down wasn’t the right move after all,” a fan said after the Dodgers lost on Thursday.
“Miss you JDP,” another commented.
“Damn JDP and will smith really carry that much weight huh,” a third added.
“Josue was only gonna get better BRING HIM BACK,” a fourth wrote.
As for the postseason, fans don’t even think it’s a question of whether De Paula should be on the team.
“Dude was on fire!! And confident!! Don’t understand at all!! And he was starting and succeeding,” a fan said.
“JDP needs to be there. He proved it!!” another chimed in.
“Cmon guys, we all know JDP will make that playoff roster, if he doesn’t I’m going to the front office myself,” a third fan said.
Safe to say, the outrage if De Paula is not on the postseason roster will be palpable.

item.title: [Dodger Blue] Dodgers manager shares opinion on Petco Park, Padres' postseason berths
item.dc:creator: Matt Borelli
item.description: The Los Angeles Dodgers and San Diego Padres just faced each other for the final time during the regular season up against a backdrop of both teams having October on their minds. item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers and San Diego Padres just faced each other for the final time during the regular season up against a backdrop of both teams having October on their minds.
The Dodgers are heading back to the playoffs for the 14th consecutive season and clinched the National League West title for a fifth year in a row. That since has been followed by securing a first-round bye in the playoffs.
Meanwhile, the Padres punched their ticket for the playoffs by defeating the Dodgers on Thursday night. The Padres are in the postseason for a franchise-record third consecutive season, and their fifth appearance in the last seven years.
“Small market, huh?” Dodgers manager Dave Roberts jokingly asked. “I think they’ve certainly accrued a lot of talent, the fanbase is very supportive, Petco is one of the best places to play a ballgame and take in a baseball game.
“I think (Craig) Stammen is great and I like what they’ve done. I think they’ve done some good things. A.J. (Preller) has done a great job. They’re always a thorn in our side and great competition.”
The Padres are often championed for their willingness to put a competitive product on the field each season despite playing in a small market. Their resurgence began under former owner Peter Seidler and is now continuing with José E. Feliciano at the helm.
The Padres haven’t been able to get over the hump to this point, but they hope that changes this year.
Under the current NL postseason bracket, San Diego would have to get past the Wild Card Series and Division Series for a potential showdown with the Dodgers in the Championship Series. The teams have met three times in MLB postseason history — all since 2020 — with L.A. winning two of those series.
Dave Roberts: Padres ‘good’ test for Dodgers
Prior to their three-game series beginning at Dodger Stadium, Roberts said the Padres being in town would present a good tuneup for the Dodgers before they head into the postseason.
“I think it’s going to be a good kind of primer,” Roberts said. “They’re a very talented team, they’re playing as good as anyone in all of baseball. I’m looking forward to playing those guys and just kind of ramping it up a little bit more for our guys.”

item.title: [FanSided] Why MLB fans should root for Roki Sasaki in the playoffs, not revel in Dodgers downfall
item.dc:creator: Jake Elman

item.content:encoded:
Crossing the Pacific Ocean and signing with the Los Angeles Dodgers meant cultural and personal transitions for prized Japanese import Roki Sasaki.
But when Sasaki officially met the U.S. media in early 2025, he made it clear he and his newest fanbase had two things in common: baseball and grief.
Sasaki returned from the injured list this week just as a March 2025 story by the Dodgers’ official website resurfaced on social media. At the time, California was still recovering from the January 2025 wildfires that ravaged the Los Angeles area, an unfortunately familiar sight for their newest pitcher.
Nearly 15 years earlier, Sasaki lost his father, grandparents, and his family’s home in the March 2011 tsunami. He turned to baseball as an escape, just as so many others affected by tragedy often do.
"Los Angeles is facing challenging and difficult times right now,” Sasaki said in January 2025, “and as a member of the Dodgers, starting today, I am dedicated to give my best and strive forward together with the people of the city."
Baseball fans can support Roki Sasaki without rooting for the Los Angeles Dodgers
This might sound contradictory, but hear us out.
We just saw Mets fans overwhelmingly cheer for Pete Alonso, even after he smashed a game-tying home run. Citi Field cared far more about Alonso the player than it did the Orioles as a team. Had the Orioles somehow snuck into the postseason, we imagine there’d be plenty of Mets fans with even the slightest rooting interest.
The same principle — or, at least, an extremely similar one — easily applies to Sasaki. Forget the fact he signed with the reigning World Series champions and played a pivotal role during last year’s title run. He’s still a human being with emotions who went through a horrifically traumatic experience; nearly 20,000 people are believed to have died in the Great East Japan Earthquake, and over 2,550 people remained missing as of 2021.
And above all else, Sasaki hasn’t done anything wrong beyond struggling to hit the strike zone. But compare that to some of the other notable names we’ll see this postseason. San Diego’s Fernando Tatis Jr. and Ramón Laureano each served PED-related suspensions. Boston’s Jarren Duran has feuded with fans and media in a way Red Sox Nation eventually stopped defending.
We’ve long been critical of both Sasaki and how the Dodgers have refused to make him a full-time reliever. Dave Roberts confirmed earlier this week the 24-year-old will pitch out of the bullpen during the postseason, just as he did last October, and the first impressions were positive; Sasaki threw a scoreless inning and didn’t allow a walk against the Padres on Tuesday night.
We wouldn’t blame you for hoping the Dodgers lose in the NLDS. They’re a superteam seeking their third consecutive championship and fourth in six years. At least three players on the active roster — Shohei Ohtani, Freddie Freeman, and Mookie Betts — are widely considered locks for the Hall of Fame, and Tarik Skubal is well on his way.
But when Sasaki comes in from the bullpen, try not to be overly hard on him. Save your vitriol for the umpires and broadcasters.

item.dc:creator: Dibyendu Mondal

item.content:encoded:
Mookie Betts batted second against the San Diego Padres on Thursday. The Los Angeles Dodgers returned Shohei Ohtani to his usual leadoff spot.
He played behind Betts on Wednesday at No. 2.
But the change didn’t see success. San Diego beat the Dodgers 4-2 on Thursday night. The win clinched the Padres’ franchise-record third consecutive postseason berth, their fifth in seven seasons.
The Dodgers also secured a bye into the Division Series, avoiding the wild-card round.
Los Angeles now turns to the San Francisco Giants to close the regular season. The three-game series opens Friday at Oracle Park and runs through Sunday. The Dodgers open the postseason on Oct. 3.
Betts went 3-for-4 with a double in Thursday’s loss. He scored a run and drew a walk. He is heating up at the perfect time. In September, his average improved to .367 from .257, with an OPS of 1.177.
Keeping up with the success on the field, Betts also announced major news off the field.
Mookie Betts Announces Major Career News
Betts signed with 3 Arts Sports and Sanders Sports & Entertainment for personal representation.
“We’re excited to announce that 3 Arts Sports and Sanders Sports & Entertainment are joining forces to represent Los Angeles Dodgers star Mookie Betts across brand partnerships, business opportunities and off-field ventures,” the two firms wrote. “Proud to be on Mookie’s team and excited for what’s ahead.”
Betts reshared the post on his own Instagram account.
The two firms will co-manage his personal endorsements, brand partnerships and business development.
3 Arts Sports also represents Travis Kelce, WNBA star Sophie Cunningham and NFL stars Jayden Daniels and Myles Garrett.
Kelce recently signed on as Tommy Hilfiger’s global brand ambassador, a multi-season deal that includes a co-designed menswear collection as a partner of 3 Arts Sports.
Betts face value sits alongside the biggest in the industry.
Shohei Ohtani is Looking Great Ahead of Postseason
Manager Dave Roberts assessed Ohtani after Wednesday’s return. He called Ohtani considerably better than before the injured list stint, roughly an 8 or 9 out of 10 compared with a 5 beforehand.
“The last 2 nights, he’s looked great,” Roberts said. “Really exciting, just missed a homer.”
Ohtani will not pitch in the postseason. The Dodgers shut him down from pitching for the rest of 2026 earlier this month. Roberts said the move lets Ohtani focus fully on hitting.

item.title: [heavy.com] Dodgers Get Encouraging Edwin Diaz News Ahead of MLB Playoffs
item.dc:creator: Keith Watkins
item.description: The Los Angeles Dodgers dropped the rubber match of their series against the San Diego Padres on Thursday, falling 4-2 in their regular season home finale at Dodger Stadium. In the ninth inning, something encouraging happened. Edwin Diaz took the mound and shut the door. The right-hander struck out two batters and allowed no hits in a clean ninth. item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers dropped the rubber match of their series against the San Diego Padres on Thursday, falling 4-2 in their regular season home finale at Dodger Stadium.
In the ninth inning, something encouraging happened. Edwin Diaz took the mound and shut the door.
The right-hander struck out two batters and allowed no hits in a clean ninth. After the game, manager Dave Roberts offered a notable assessment of where Diaz stands heading into October.
Roberts on Diaz’s Recent Run
Roberts has watched Diaz closely since returning from the injured list. Each outing has looked better than the last.
“This has been the best of the 4,” Roberts said of Diaz’s performance. “He’ll pitch 1 of the games this weekend, 7th, 8th or 9th.”
Diaz kept it simple when asked what has been working.
“I was throwing strikes,” Diaz said. “That’s my goal.”
The Road Back for Diaz
Diaz’s 2026 season nearly ended before it began. He underwent surgery in late April to remove loose bodies from his right elbow, an injury that put him on the 60-day injured list and cast doubt on whether he would pitch again this year.
His early-season numbers before the surgery were ugly. But the version of Diaz that has returned looks far closer to the pitcher who posted a 1.63 ERA with a 0.87 WHIP for the New York Mets in 2025, ranking second among qualified relievers with a 38 percent strikeout rate.
The Dodgers signed Diaz knowing his ceiling. Getting that ceiling back in September, right before October, changes the complexion of their bullpen.
Final Word for the Dodgers
Edwin Diaz came to Los Angeles to close games in October. Elbow surgery and a lost summer threatened to erase that plan entirely.
Now, the plan is back. Roberts is giving him the ball in the seventh, eighth, or ninth. The strikeouts are coming. The strikes are landing.
The Dodgers’ postseason is approaching. Diaz intends to be a factor. Based on what Roberts said Thursday, the Dodgers believe him.

item.title: [The Sporting Tribune] Glasnow delivers strong final tune-up despite Dodgers loss
item.dc:creator: Fredo Cervantes
item.description: LOS ANGELES — Tyler Glasnow walked off the mound Thursday night having done almost everything the Dodgers could have asked of him. The result, however, belonged to the Padres. Glasnow carried a no-hit bid into the sixth inning and struck out 11 over 6⅓ innings in his final tune-up before the postseason, but the Padres broke through late and held on to beat the Dodgers, 4-2, in the final home game of the 2026 regular season at Uniqlo Field at Dodger Stadium.
