item.content:encoded:
Dodgers news: What Dave Roberts said about Shohei Ohtani's 1st game back from IL appeared first on ClutchPoints. Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here.
Los Angeles Dodgers designated hitter Shohei Ohtani returned to the lineup Wednesday after spending two weeks on the injured list.
Ohtani was activated before Los Angeles' 5-1 loss to the San Diego Padres after missing time because of left knee soreness and right biceps discomfort. It was his first game since Sept. 7, and he was inserted into the No. 2 spot against Padres left-hander Robbie Ray.
The 32-year-old finished 1-for-4 with a walk and two strikeouts. His first at-bat ended with a 99 mph single to right field, and he later hit a 384-foot flyout to center. His biggest missed opportunity came in the fourth inning, when he struck out with the bases loaded during the Dodgers' best scoring chance.
Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)
Despite the result, manager Dave Roberts came away encouraged by what he saw from Ohtani.
"He looked good. I thought the at-bat quality was good," said Roberts. "There wasn't any chase. I thought he hit the ball hardest in his first at-bat. It's been a while since he's played in a game, but it just felt like he wasn't sped up at all."
In his final games before landing on the IL, Ohtani had appeared physically compromised at the plate, including moments when he shook out his arm and winced. Los Angeles placed him on the injured list on Sept. 9 after trying to manage the lingering issues while keeping him available.
Ohtani had begun his hitting program about a week before Wednesday's return and had recently faced simulated pitching. He had entered his last game before the IL stint batting .277 with 30 home runs, 80 RBIs, 89 runs and 80 walks through 134 games.
Roberts said Ohtani is expected to return to the lineup Thursday for the series finale. The Dodgers are also still evaluating their batting order against left-handed pitching for the postseason. Against right-handers, Roberts said he would likely put Ohtani back in the leadoff spot and move Mookie Betts to No. 2.
Betts had occupied the leadoff role while Ohtani was away and was batting .366 with six homers, 21 RBIs, 13 walks and 18 runs in 18 September games.
Ohtani won't take the mound in the playoffs, making his health at the plate all the more important as October approaches.
Related: Shohei Ohtani, Tarik Skubal set to return to Dodgers

item.title: [nypost.com] Shohei Ohtani is back — but something doesn’t look right with Dodgers star
item.dc:creator: Dylan Hernandez
item.description: Something’s not right. The Dodgers said so without saying so. When Shohei Ohtani returned from the 15-day injured list, they batted him second. This is no knock on Mookie Betts, who led off instead. Betts is an eight-time All-Star who is hitting .317 over his last 42 games, but Ohtani is, well, Ohtani. Ohtani is the best player in baseball when healthy, or even close to healthy. If the Dodgers believed Ohtani could be that player for them in the postseason, they wouldn’t have moved him out of hi
item.content:encoded:
Something’s not right.
The Dodgers said so without saying so.
When Shohei Ohtani returned from the 15-day injured list, they batted him second.
This is no knock on Mookie Betts, who led off instead. Betts is an eight-time All-Star who is hitting .317 over his last 42 games, but Ohtani is, well, Ohtani.
Ohtani is the best player in baseball when healthy, or even close to healthy. If the Dodgers believed Ohtani could be that player for them in the postseason, they wouldn’t have moved him out of his customary spot in the order, and it wouldn’t have mattered how anyone else on their team was hitting or whether the opposing pitcher was right- and left-handed.
Presumably, the Dodgers had more insights into his injured right arm and left knee than they shared.
Which is why enthusiasm over Ohtani’s performance on Wednesday should be tempered.
Without question, Ohtani looked better in the 5-1 loss to the San Diego Padres than he did the last time he played.
That didn’t mean he was back to playing like himself – or that he will be at any time during the playoffs.
The return of a Most Valuable Player can have transformative effects on a team, especially if that Most Valuable Player is as healthy as the Dodgers claimed Ohtani was after resting for two-plus weeks, but President of Baseball Operations Andrew Friedman and manager Dave Roberts both spent time before the game managing expectations.
Asked which version of Ohtani was coming back to the team, Friedman replied, “I mean, these aren’t things there’s a clear answer to.”
Roberts said he wanted to see Ohtani “being controlled, taking good at-bats.”
By that standard, Ohtani’s first game back was a massive triumph.
In the first inning, Ohtani singled off left-hander Robbie Ray on the kind of low pitch he was physically incapable of reaching two or three weeks earlier because of his knee problem.
Ohtani later drove a high 99-mph fastball to the warning track, prompting Dodgers broadcaster Joe Davis to scream: “That is a majestic fly ball!”
“I think if you look back at the last couple weeks when he was active, he wasn’t getting to that pitch,” Roberts said of the four-seamer upstairs from right-hander Bradgley Rodriguez.
For the most part, Ohtani didn’t swing at pitches outside of the strike zone. He worked two-ball counts in each of his first four plate appearances, and drew a walk in the third inning.
The Dodgers would almost certainly take games like this from Ohtani. Regardless of what he actually was and wasn’t able to do, the Padres viewed him as a threat, and that alone made him a presence in the lineup.
Ohtani has acknowledged he was unlikely to be 100% healthy again this season, but maintaining an aura of danger will require him to not return to where he was physically leading up to his IL stint.
“Shohei says he feels back to where he was earlier in the year, which is great, which is a good start,” Friedman said. “Now, it’s one thing to feel that way for any player coming back from the IL. When you’re coming back, now the question is, as you start to load on real games and that intensity and that workload, it’s making sure that what we’re done keeps guys in position to be at their best.”
Or, in this case, to at least be viewed as a threat.
Roberts previously described Ohtani as “pain-free” but acknowledged he was still dealing with “discomfort you can play through.” The Dodgers have already seen what happens when Ohtani plays too many games with his arm and knee problems, and every game he plays theoretically pushes him closer to the stage at which the pain becomes unbearable.
How close is Ohtani to that point?
Was the usually-aggressive Ohtani as patient as he was in the batter’s box because he wanted to protect his arm by limiting his swings?
Did his warning-track drive not clear the outfield wall because he hit the ball with the end of his bat or because he wasn’t at full strength?
What should be made of the two at-bats in which he struck out? With the bases loaded, two outs and the count full in the fourth inning, Ohtani was late on a 98.5-mph sinker by David Morgan. In the ninth, Ohtani looked as if he had no chance against closer Mason Miller, who struck him out on three pitches.
Ohtani wasn’t made available to answer any of these questions. By the time the clubhouse opened to reporters, Ohtani was gone.

item.title: [Dodgers Nation] Josue De Paula Earns Rave Reviews From Dodgers Leadership
item.dc:creator: Nelson Espinal
item.description: Los Angeles Dodgers top prospect Josue De Paula is no longer on the active roster after getting sent down to Triple-A, but the major league team had nothing but positive things to say. De Paula played just 11 games with the Dodgers, but he delivered outstanding offensive production and quickly earned the fanbase’s adoration as a young presence at the plate. However, he was demoted as Shohei Ohtani neared activation from the injured list. Fans who bought into what the 21-year-old showed were disa
item.content:encoded:
Los Angeles Dodgers top prospect Josue De Paula is no longer on the active roster after getting sent down to Triple-A, but the major league team had nothing but positive things to say.
De Paula played just 11 games with the Dodgers, but he delivered outstanding offensive production and quickly earned the fanbase’s adoration as a young presence at the plate.
However, he was demoted as Shohei Ohtani neared activation from the injured list. Fans who bought into what the 21-year-old showed were disappointed, but the organization seemed just as reluctant to see him go.
What the Dodgers think of De Paula
After the move was announced, manager Dave Roberts said De Paula, as the team’s default designated hitter, was set to lose at-bats now that Ohtani returned.
Still, De Paula earned a postseason look, and the team will factor him into its plans.
“We had a runway to give him, which we gave him, and he performed more than admirably. He’s a part of the conversation, and he’s earned that, and that’s what I told him last night,” Roberts said to the media, including Dodgers Nation’s Noel Sanchez.
In terms of skill set, Roberts sees all of De Paul’s traits — the plate approach, swing decision, and vision to deliver in the postseason.
“He’s just a special hitter,” Roberts added. “Hitters don’t see the ball that quickly out of hand; it’s a gift. Just the ability to [limit] chase, I think that lines up in the postseason. And no moment is going to be too big for that kid.”
De Paula’s impressive numbers
Through 11 games in the big leagues, De Paul is hitting .323/.500/.545 with a 1.081 OPS. He is getting on base during half of his plate appearances, and he is really making hitters work.
Andrew Friedman, the president of baseball operations, had been following De Paula closely, and despite the otherworldly production, the Dodgers executive was not surprised.
“It’s what you expect, but you never really know until you see it,” Friedman said to the media, including Dodgers Nation.
“But it obviously really stood out, and he’s done everything he can to put himself in a position to be in the conversation for us as we’re making our postseason roster.”
Meanwhile, Josue De Paula gets the chance to show what he can do defensively in Triple-A while the Dodgers decide.

item.title: [Field Level Media] Dodgers, Padres clash with postseason goals within reach
item.description: The Los Angeles Dodgers and San Diego Padres will say farewell for now in their final meeting of the regular season Thursday night in L.A., with one team guaranteed to celebrate at the end of the evening. In the finale of the next-to-last series for each team, the Padres have a magic number of one for clinching a National League wild-card spot, while the Dodgers have a magic number of one to earn a top-two seed in the playoffs and a bye into a division series matchup. There even remains a chance
item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers and San Diego Padres will say farewell for now in their final meeting of the regular season Thursday night in L.A., with one team guaranteed to celebrate at the end of the evening.
In the finale of the next-to-last series for each team, the Padres have a magic number of one for clinching a National League wild-card spot, while the Dodgers have a magic number of one to earn a top-two seed in the playoffs and a bye into a division series matchup.
There even remains a chance that both achieve their objectives depending on other results throughout the NL.
As it stands now, the Dodgers (97-61) and Padres (88-70) could collide again in a division-series matchup. The Padres earned a 5-1 victory Wednesday to end the Dodgers’ 11-game home winning streak, while the Dodgers won 7-0 on Tuesday.
The Padres have won 14 of their past 16 games.
A pair of right-handers will match up in the final game of the series as San Diego sends Nick Pivetta (3-2, 3.30 ERA) to the mound, while Los Angeles will counter with Tyler Glasnow (5-1, 3.46).
Pivetta will have history on the line. The Padres have never reached the playoffs in three consecutive seasons. In three starts since a five-month stint on the injured list because of a right elbow flexor strain, Pivetta is 2-0 with a 1.93 ERA.
In eight career appearances against the Dodgers (seven starts), he is 1-2 with a 3.62 ERA.
Pivetta has yet to go more than five innings since his return, but he will have additional bullpen support with the return of right-hander Jason Adam, who has been out since June with a shoulder injury.
“What this team’s doing is really special,” Adam said, according to the San Diego Union-Tribune. “I just want to fill my role, however that looks, and help them win ballgames. We’ve seen that this team’s good with or without me. I just want to do my part to contribute.”
The Dodgers saw Shohei Ohtani return from a biceps injury Wednesday, and he reached base in his first two at-bats on a single and a walk. But he struck out with the bases loaded in the fourth inning against right-hander David Morgan.
“He looked good,” Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said of Ohtani. “At-bat quality was good. There wasn’t any chase. I thought he hit the ball hard in his first at-bat, just missed a homer (in the seventh inning), took a walk. It was good. It’s been a while since he’s played in a game, but it felt like he wasn’t sped up at all.”
Ohtani hit out of the No. 2 spot in the lineup against left-hander Robbie Ray, while Mookie Betts remained the leadoff hitter for the fifth consecutive game. Ohtani is expected to play again Thursday and might return to the leadoff spot against Pivetta.
Glasnow is 2-1 with a 4.50 ERA in five starts since returning from a back injury. In his most recent outing Friday against the San Francisco Giants, he had a season-high 10 strikeouts in earning an 8-2 win.
In eight career appearances against San Diego (five starts), Glasnow is 0-1 with a 3.27 ERA.
–Field Level Media

item.title: [Dodgers Nation] Hyeseong Kim Makes His Case for Dodgers' Postseason Roster
item.dc:creator: Cameron Kiszla
item.description: Utility player Hyeseong Kim is giving the Los Angeles Dodgers something to think about as they’re putting together the postseason roster. Kim, who’s been with the Oklahoma City Comets since May, went 2-for-4 in Game 2 of the Pacific Coast League Championship Series Wednesday night. Kim’s night also included a double, an RBI and a run scored in the Comets’ 7-1 win over the Las Vegas Aviators, a victory that forces a deciding Game 3 on Thursday. It came on the heels of another 2-for-4 game for Kim
item.content:encoded:
Utility player Hyeseong Kim is giving the Los Angeles Dodgers something to think about as they’re putting together the postseason roster.
Kim, who’s been with the Oklahoma City Comets since May, went 2-for-4 in Game 2 of the Pacific Coast League Championship Series Wednesday night.
Kim’s night also included a double, an RBI and a run scored in the Comets’ 7-1 win over the Las Vegas Aviators, a victory that forces a deciding Game 3 on Thursday.
It came on the heels of another 2-for-4 game for Kim on Tuesday night in which he also scored two runs, a sign of progress amid a largely uneven season at the plate.
How has Hyeseong Kim played in 2026?
Kim’s production at the major-league and minor-league levels has been virtually identical in 2026, and not in a way that shows Kim living up to his potential.
In the majors, he hit .259 with one home run and 11 RBIs.
In the minors, where he’s spent about triple the time, he is hitting .262 with three homers and 31 RBIs.
He has also stolen five bases in the majors and 15 in the minors.
While the production hasn’t necessarily been eye-popping, his skills could be a huge boon to the Dodgers in the playoffs, something manager Dave Roberts addressed recently.
What do the Dodgers plan to do with Hyeseong Kim?
Roberts said that the Dodgers plan to use next week, when they are almost assuredly going to get a bye for the wild card round, to meet with Kim and possibly add him to the postseason roster.
“My expectation is that Kim will be here during the off week and potentially be in the conversation for the postseason, because he has the ability to run and play defense and steal a base,” he said.
That said, those offensive numbers that Kim has put up in Triple-A and the majors this season give Roberts and the Dodgers coaches and executives pause, he said.
“I think for Hyeseong, it’s the at bat consistency,” Roberts said. “I don’t think that his offense has been consistent.”
Especially compared to some of the other players who are fighting for a playoff roster spot, Kim’s relative inconsistency could spell doom for his postseason hopes.
“For us, the at bat quality, for example, that Alex Freeland is giving us has been very good,” Roberts said. “He gets on base. I think for Hyeseong, just trying to find something consistent and perform consistently. And to be quite frank, he just hasn’t been as consistent as he can be. But if he can get more consistent with the bat, then he can be a big piece.”
Dodgers fans will find out in the coming days if Kim has indeed done enough to earn a spot for October, but his supporters can rest assured that he’s putting his best foot forward in these Triple-A playoffs.

item.title: [truebluela.com] Dodgers notes: Postseason bullpen in a good spot
item.dc:creator: Andy Lane Chapman
item.description: Tuesday night’s game against the San Diego Padres was reminiscent of the 2024 playoffs when the Dodgers were forced to employ a bullpen in the NLDS to keep their playoff hopes alive against those same Padres. Both outcomes were the same, with the bullpen shutting down the Friars and getting a big win. That postseason saw a lot of bullpen usage, and in this one the Dodgers are stacked with starters. Still, the bullpen is always a big part of the postseason. As Fabian Ardaya of The Athletic points
item.content:encoded:
Tuesday night’s game against the San Diego Padres was reminiscent of the 2024 playoffs when the Dodgers were forced to employ a bullpen in the NLDS to keep their playoff hopes alive against those same Padres. Both outcomes were the same, with the bullpen shutting down the Friars and getting a big win.
That postseason saw a lot of bullpen usage, and in this one the Dodgers are stacked with starters. Still, the bullpen is always a big part of the postseason.
As Fabian Ardaya of The Athletic points out, 41 days ago manager Dave Roberts was asking the media what choices did he truly have to deploy in the ninth inning of games. Now, he could have several options.
Edwin Diaz, the closer they paid handsomely in the offseason, has not had a great season. He’s been on the IL twice and had an era over 11.00 at one point this summer. But since returning from his latest IL stint, he has faced 11 batters, struck out six and only allowed two to reach base.
“I think it’s one of those things where if you’re one of the 12 pitchers on a postseason roster, you’re in the trust tree,” Roberts said “He’s put himself right smack in that conversation. Given all that he’s had to go through this year to right the ship is a big credit to him.”
Roki Sasaki is also someone who will be in the mix for the ninth inning spot. He has also just returned from his own IL stint, pitching with dermabond on his blister. He allowed two singles, but worked around them for a scoreless inning in Tuesday night’s game. He will appear in Friday night’s game as he continues to work towards a spot in the bullpen that will likely vary as the postseason goes on.
Tanner Scott has been the Dodgers’ most reliable arm out of the bullpen this season, and Roberts has remarked how it would be nice to be able to use Scott in high leverage spots that may not come just in the ninth inning.
“I think if there’s an opportunity, for example, for Tanner to pitch a high-leverage inning in the seventh or the eighth inning, it’s just hard to pass that up if he’s the best option right there,” Roberts said. “You just don’t know where the ninth inning is going to be.”
Roberts also added that the team is sitting in their best position with regards to the bullpen as they have ever been. Evan Phillips and Brock Stewart round out the current options, and the team hopes that Edguardo Henriquez can recover from his back issues to appear in the playoffs. With the starters this team has overall this may be the best pitching staff the Dodgers have ever sent to the playoffs.

item.title: [nbclosangeles.com] Ohtani returns to Dodgers lineup and delivers hit in first at-bat
item.dc:creator: Associated Press
item.description: Shohei Ohtani got a hit in his return to the Los Angeles Dodgers' lineup on Wednesday night after missing two weeks with right biceps discomfort. He batted second as the designated hitter against the San Diego Padres and left-handed starter Robbie Ray. Ohtani hits left-handed and throws and pitches right-handed. “I’m not expecting too much,” manager Dave Roberts said before the game. “It’s been a while since he’s played, but it’s just good to get him in there.” A roar went up from Dodger fans as
item.content:encoded:
Shohei Ohtani got a hit in his return to the Los Angeles Dodgers' lineup on Wednesday night after missing two weeks with right biceps discomfort.
He batted second as the designated hitter against the San Diego Padres and left-handed starter Robbie Ray. Ohtani hits left-handed and throws and pitches right-handed.
“I’m not expecting too much,” manager Dave Roberts said before the game. “It’s been a while since he’s played, but it’s just good to get him in there.”
A roar went up from Dodger fans as Ohtani walked to the plate to Michael Bublé's “Feeling Good.” He promptly lined a 2-1 pitch from Ray into right field and the fans got loud again. Ohtani was out at second base when Will Smith grounded into a fielder's choice to third.
Mookie Betts was in Ohtani's usual leadoff spot, where he's been since the two-way superstar went on the injured list on Sept. 8.
Betts is hitting .366 with six home runs, 21 RBIs, 13 walks and 18 runs scored in 18 games in September. He's tied for third in the major leagues with 26 hits this month, and also ranks among National League leaders this month in extra-base hits, RBIs, total bases, doubles and runs.
Ohtani last played on Sept. 7 against Cincinnati and came in hitting .277 with 30 homers, 80 RBIs, 89 runs scored and 80 walks in 134 games. He appeared physically compromised at the plate, shaking out his arm and wincing at times.
Local
Get Los Angeles's latest local news on crime, entertainment, weather, schools, cost of living and more. Here's your go-to source for today's LA news.
“A few weeks ago you could see that he couldn’t hit a fastball, he was underneath everything and it was a slower swing,” Roberts said. “Just controlling the swing, the barrel, I think that’s something I’ll look at and obviously stuff like the wincing, but I don’t expect to see any of that.”
Roberts said he likely would have Ohtani leading off and Betts hitting second against right-handed pitching.
The Dodgers conclude their three-game set against the Padres on Thursday, then head to San Francisco for three games against the Giants to end the regular season.
Roberts expects to see a focused Ohtani at the plate.
“It’s go-time for all of us and I think he’s in a good spot,” Roberts said. “He's getting ready for the postseason. His mind should be there and my bet is that that’s where it’s at.”
In other moves, pitcher Tarik Skubal was reinstated from the bereavement list. He is scheduled to start Friday at San Francisco. Reliever Kyle Hurt was optioned to Triple-A Oklahoma City.
Rookie Josue De Paula sent back to minors, could return for postseason
With Ohtani's return, Josue De Paula was sent down to Triple-A to join the Comets in the Pacific Coast League playoffs against the Las Vegas Aviators. De Paula had been in the lineup as the DH.
De Paula quickly became a fan favorite during Ohtani's absence. The 21-year-old New York native reached base safely in 10 of his first 11 games in the majors. He went 2 for 3 with a run scored and a walk while notching his first career triple in the Dodgers' 7-0 win over the Padres on Tuesday.
“He performed more than admirably,” Roberts said. “This also just gives us an opportunity to potentially have him back for the postseason. He’s a part of the conversation and he’s earned that, and that’s what I told him.”
If De Paula makes the postseason roster, he would serve as a pinch-hitter.
“Josue has been awesome,” said Andrew Friedman, president of baseball operations. “Injected some real life and energy into our team.”

item.title: [Los Angeles Times] Shohei Ohtani gets a hit in his return, but Dodgers fall to the Padres

item.content:encoded:
Shohei Ohtani gets a hit in his return, but Dodgers fall to the Padres
Shohei Ohtani’s swing was a little out in front of a slider delivered by Padres left-hander Robbie Ray. But Ohtani held back his hands long enough to extend them to the pitch and shoot it through the right side of the infield.
It wasn’t flashy. But considering it was his first at-bat in over two weeks, in a tough matchup no less, it was a promising sign.
The good news quickly dried up for the Dodgers after that, as they fell to the Padres 5-1, missing a chance to clinch a first-round bye with a win. But Ohtani’s return was still significant, and the success of his end-of-season tune-up will have playoff implications.
The Dodgers activated Ohtani, who went one-for-four Wednesday, from the 15-day IL before the game and optioned rookie Josue De Paula to Triple-A. De Paula is still under consideration for the National League Division Series roster as a bat of the bench.
“This was the original thought, that once Shohei gets back, we’re going to send him out,” manager Dave Roberts said. “We had a runway to give him, which we gave him and he performed more than admirably. This also, as far as the timing, just gives us an opportunity to potentially have him back for the postseason. He’s a part of the conversation, and he’s earned that, and that’s what I told him last night.”
It was Josue De Paula’s bat that earned him a call-up when Shohei Ohtani landed on the IL. And it’s his bat that’s now making his case for a postseason roster spot.
De Paula joined triple-A Oklahoma City for Game 2 of the PCL Championship on Wednesday. And Ohtani slid into the Dodgers lineup, hitting second in the batting order for the first time this season, with Mookie Betts leading off against the Padres southpaw.
“I know Shohei, Mookie, they’re always on board with whatever I decide to do,” Roberts said. “I think it just makes it tougher to navigate versus left. There’s a Mookie tax [to get to Ohtani]. If you want to get to Freddie [Freeman], there’s a Will Smith tax. I like that. And versus a right hander I like kind of flipping those two for the same reasons.”
Ohtani, welcomed back in his first at-bat by a partial standing ovation, walked in his second plate appearance. And with two out and the bases loaded in the bottom of the fourth inning, he appeared to have walked again.
Then Padres catcher Ethan Salas tapped the top of his head to challenge the ball call. And an ABS review showed the fastball had clipped the top of the strike zone. Ohtani fouled off the next two pitches before whiffing on a sinker to end the inning.
That missed opportunity rolled right into a sloppy fifth inning for the Dodgers defense.
Starting pitcher Yoshinobu Yamamoto had given up a two-run homer to Manny Machado the previous inning but had otherwise avoided damage.
To open the fifth, he induced Salas to hit the ball on the ground, but it got away from second baseman Tommy Edman as he dove up the middle, for a single.
Yamamoto then got a soft grounder out of Fernando Tatís Jr. But it was too soft, giving Tatís time to reach first before third baseman Max Muncy could get off a throw.
With runners on first and second, Yamamoto had a chance to contribute on defense, fielding Dustin Harris’ comebacker bunt. But Yamamoto’s throw to third sailed wide, allowing a run to score. Machado then made it a 4-1 game with a sacrifice fly.
Ohtani came up to the plate again in the seventh inning and put Dodgers fans on the edge of their seats by sending a long fly ball to straightaway center field. But the cheers died down as it fell shy well short of the 395-foot wall.
The top of the Dodgers order got one last chance to start a rally in the ninth inning, against star closer Mason Miller. Only Will Smith reached base, on a walk, and advanced to third on defensive indifference. Ohtani struck out on a slider.
“[Ohtani] certainly feels way better with the rest,” president of baseball operations Andrew Friedman said before the game. “The biggest thing with five games to go is get him as many at-bats as we can, some rhythm and timing.”
Ohtani could get a day off in that span, Friedman said, but the Dodgers will make those decisions based on how he’s feeling.
After defeating the Padres, the Dodgers have five games left to round into playoff form. They get a big piece, Shohei Ohtani, back Wednesday.
“Just getting as many at-bats as he can and that rhythm and timing back before we head into October is going to be really helpful,” Friedman said.
Ohtani was not in rhythm before he landed on the IL. In the last three weeks before the Dodgers finally shelved him, he had a .130 batting average. And he only had two hits in his last seven games (26 at-bats) before the move.
“You end up making subconscious adjustments where you’re protecting yourself,” Friedman said, “and there’s just slight degradation as that’s happening that compounds over time.”

item.title: [sbsun.com] Shohei Ohtani returns to Dodgers’ lineup – but in a new spot
item.dc:creator: Bill Plunkett
item.description: LOS ANGELES — Rested and refreshed, Shohei Ohtani returned to the Dodgers’ roster on Wednesday. How refreshed remains to be seen. “These aren’t things that there’s a clear answer to,” Dodgers president of baseball operations Andrew Friedman said after Ohtani was activated from the injured list before Wednesday’s game. “I think everyone, this time of year, is dealing with some stuff, and so it’s all on that continuum. Shohei says he feels back to where he was earlier in the year, which is great,
item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES — Rested and refreshed, Shohei Ohtani returned to the Dodgers’ roster on Wednesday.
How refreshed remains to be seen.
“These aren’t things that there’s a clear answer to,” Dodgers president of baseball operations Andrew Friedman said after Ohtani was activated from the injured list before Wednesday’s game. “I think everyone, this time of year, is dealing with some stuff, and so it’s all on that continuum. Shohei says he feels back to where he was earlier in the year, which is great, which is a good start.
“Now, it’s one thing to feel that way for any player coming back from the IL. As they are coming back, it’s important for them to feel that way and when you’re coming back, now the question is, as you start to load on real games and that intensity and that workload, it’s making sure that what we’ve done keeps guys in position to be at their best.”
Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said Ohtani is “considerably” closer to being at his best than he was before going on the IL two weeks ago with biceps and knee issues.
“I would say if he was a ‘5’, he’s probably an ‘8’ or a ‘9’ right now,” Roberts said.
He also returned as a ‘2.’
For the first time since Mookie Betts suffered a fractured hand when he was hit by a pitch on June 16, 2024, Roberts wrote Ohtani’s name in as the No. 2 hitter in the Dodgers’ lineup behind Betts.
Roberts said he plans to go with Betts-Ohtani against left-handed pitching (like the Padres’ Wednesday starter, Robbie Ray) and switch to Ohtani-Betts against right-handed pitching (like Thursday’s starter, Nick Pivetta).
“I just feel good about it,” Roberts said of the decision to use both players at leadoff. “It just makes it tougher to navigate versus left(-handed pitching). There’s a Mookie tax. If you want to get to Freddie (Freeman, batting fourth), there’s a Will Smith tax. I like that and versus a right-hander I like kind of flipping those two for the same reasons.”
In four starts as the leadoff hitter before Ohtani returned, Betts was 8 for 16 with four doubles and two home runs.
Overall, the Dodgers went 10-3 in the 13 games Ohtani missed.
SEE YOU SOON
In order to make room for Ohtani on the active roster, rookie outfielder Josue De Paula was sent to Triple-A Oklahoma City, where he made his Triple-A debut Wednesday night in OKC’s playoff game against Las Vegas.
De Paula is expected to rejoin the Dodgers for next week’s bye week and is still in the running for a spot on the postseason roster. Given a “runway” to get at-bats at DH in Ohtani’s absence, De Paula went 10 for 31 (.323) with five extra-base hits (three doubles, a triple and a home run). Perhaps most impressive, he walked 11 times in 42 plate appearances while striking out just five times.
“It was actually an easier conversation than you guys probably would expect, given how well he’s performed,” Roberts said of telling De Paula he was being sent back to the minors – however briefly.
“This was the original thought that once Shohei gets back, we’re going to send him out. We had a runway to give him, which we gave him and he performed more than admirably.”
By sending De Paula out on Wednesday, he will be eligible to be recalled in time for the first game of a best-of-five National League Division Series next week.
“He’s a part of the conversation and he’s earned that and that’s what I told him last night,” Roberts said.
Roberts said De Paula showed in his short audition that he is “a special hitter.”
“Doesn’t chase. Moves the ball forward. The threat of power. Lefties don’t faze him,” Roberts recounted. “Hitters don’t (usually) see the ball that quickly out of hand. It’s a gift. No moment is going to be too big for that kid (if he is on the postseason roster).”
PITCHING PLANS
In addition to activating Ohtani on Wednesday, the Dodgers activated starting pitcher Tarik Skubal from the bereavement list and sent right-handed reliever Kyle Hurt back to Triple-A.
Skubal is scheduled to make his final regular-season start on Friday night in San Francisco. Blake Snell came out of his bullpen session on Tuesday with no issues in the groin injury that forced him to leave his start last week after one inning. He is expected to start Saturday’s game in San Francisco as a final test before the postseason.
UP NEXT
Padres (RHP Nick Pivetta, 3-2, 3.30 ERA) at Dodgers (RHP Tyler Glasnow, 5-1, 3.46 ERA), Thursday, 7:10 p.m., SportsNet LA, TBS, 570 AM

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Josue De Paula sent down by Dodgers but 'special hitter' could still factor into playoff plans
item.dc:creator: Andrés Soto; USA TODAY
item.description: LOS ANGELES — Josue De Paula's first trial run in the big leagues has come to an end. For now, at least. With Shohei Ohtani back in the lineup for the Los Angeles Dodgers on Wednesday, Sept. 23 against the San Diego Padres and manager Dave Roberts wanting to get a look at other players competing for a spot on the postseason roster, Roberts said the choice to option De Paula to Triple-A Oklahoma City was easier than it might've appeared on the surface. "This was the original thought," Roberts sai
item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES — Josue De Paula's first trial run in the big leagues has come to an end. For now, at least.
With Shohei Ohtani back in the lineup for the Los Angeles Dodgers on Wednesday, Sept. 23 against the San Diego Padres and manager Dave Roberts wanting to get a look at other players competing for a spot on the postseason roster, Roberts said the choice to option De Paula to Triple-A Oklahoma City was easier than it might've appeared on the surface.
"This was the original thought," Roberts said. "That once Shohei gets back, we were going to send (De Paula) out. We had a runway to give him, which we gave him, and he performed more than admirably."
Even that might be an understatement to how well De Paula played.
In a small sample size of 11 games, the 21-year-old showed a confidence and poise beyond his years in the batter's box, controlling the strike zone like a seasoned vet and drawing 11 walks. And once the hits started falling, De Paula showed how dangerous he can really be, mashing three doubles and a home run (his first MLB hit in Miami) while driving in seven RBIs and posting a 1.081 OPS across 31 at-bats. His last regular season game in LA on Tuesday may have been his best yet as De Paula went 2-for-3 with a walk and his first career triple in a 7-0, series-opening win over the Padres.
He's played so well, in fact, that Roberts is seriously considering him for the postseason roster.
"He's a part of that conversation," Roberts said. "He's earned that."
De Paula's value goes beyond the stat sheet, too. Whether he's flipping the bat and yelling, "I really do this!" to his teammates in the dugout after hitting his first career home run, flexing after driving in a go-ahead run on a double or just nodding his head after not chasing a ball outside the zone, there's a level of swag De Paula brings to Dodger Stadium that not only energizes his older teammates, but also captivates fans in attendance every time "Hypnotize" by The Notorious B.I.G. blares over the loudspeakers when the Brooklyn native walks up to the plate.
Per MLB rules, a player who has been optioned can be eligible to play in the postseason as long as his club did so at least 10 days before a series. Optioning De Paula Wednesday would make him eligible to play in the NLDS, Game 1 of which starts on Saturday, Oct. 3, exactly 10 days from now.
That gives the Dodgers flexibility to evaluate the rest of the players vying for a spot in October with limited at-bats to go around in their remaining five games. Roberts specifically mentioned that he wants to get more reps for Miguel Rojas and Kiké Hernández, but the player that De Paula is most directly competing with is probably Dalton Rushing. He's been on the IL since Sept. 5 with right elbow discomfort but is expected to be activated ahead of the final regular season series in San Francisco this weekend.
Rushing won't catch again this season, so his best shot at making the playoff roster is as a lefty bat off the bench, which is the role De Paula would also have, given that president of baseball operations Andrew Friedman mentioned they currently view De Paula as a DH until his defense develops and he can be the capable corner outfielder they believe he can be one day. The Dodgers are unlikely to carry both De Paula and Rushing in October.
But while Rushing, Rojas and Hernández try to make their case in the last few opportunities, De Paula's already made his impression on Dodgers brass.
"Josue's been awesome," Friedman said. "Injected some real-life energy into our team as we got into September and close out the regular season. He handled himself as well as he could possibly do. ... He's done everything he can to put himself in a position to be in the conversation for us as we make our postseason roster."
"He's just a special hitter," Roberts said. "Hitters don't see the ball that quickly out of hand. It's a gift. Just the ability to (not) chase, I think that lines up in the postseason and no moment's gonna be too big for that kid."
De Paula joins the Comets in the middle of the Triple-A playoffs, but Roberts has basically seen enough from the rookie. The onus now lies on the vets.
This article originally appeared on USA TODAY: Josue De Paula sent down by Dodgers but 'special hitter' could still factor into playoff plans

item.content:encoded:
Por BETH HARRIS
LOS ÁNGELES (AP) — Shohei Ohtani conectó un hit en su regreso a la alineación de los Dodgers de Los Ángeles la noche del miércoles, después de perderse dos semanas por molestias en el bíceps derecho.
Bateó segundo como bateador designado contra el abridor zurdo de los Padres de San Diego Robbie Ray.
“No estoy esperando demasiado. Ha pasado un tiempo desde que juega, pero es bueno tenerlo ahí”, comentó el mánager Dave Roberts antes del juego.
Los aficionados ovacionaron a Ohtani cuando caminó hacia el plato con “Feeling Good”, de Michael Bublé. De inmediato conectó una línea al jardín derecho con un lanzamiento de Ray en cuenta de 2-1 y los aficionados volvieron a alborotarse. Ohtani fue puesto out en segunda base cuando Will Smith bateó un rodado para una jugada de selección del fildeador hacia tercera.
Mookie Betts estuvo en el puesto habitual de primer bate de Ohtani, donde ha estado desde que la superestrella ingresó a la lista de lesionados el 8 de septiembre.
Betts batea para .366 con seis jonrones, 21 carreras impulsadas, 13 bases por bolas y 18 carreras anotadas en 18 juegos en septiembre. Está empatado en el tercer lugar de las Grandes Ligas con 26 hits este mes, y también figura entre los líderes de la Liga Nacional este mes en hits de extrabase, carreras impulsadas, bases totales, dobles y carreras anotadas.
Ohtani jugó por última vez el 7 de septiembre contra Cincinnati y llegó bateando para .277 con 30 jonrones, 80 carreras impulsadas, 89 carreras anotadas y 80 bases por bolas en 134 juegos. En el plato se le vio físicamente limitado, sacudiendo el brazo y haciendo gestos de dolor en ocasiones.
“Hace unas semanas se podía ver que no podía batear una recta; se quedaba por debajo de todo y el swing era más lento”, señaló Roberts. “Controlar el swing, el punto de contacto, creo que eso es algo en lo que me fijaré y, obviamente, cosas como los gestos de dolor, pero no espero ver nada de eso”.
Los Dodgers concluyen su serie de tres juegos contra los Padres el jueves, y luego viajan a San Francisco para tres juegos contra los Giants para cerrar la temporada regular.
En otros movimientos, el lanzador Tarik Skubal fue reincorporado desde la lista por duelo. Está programado para abrir el viernes en San Francisco. El relevista Kyle Hurt fue enviado a Triple-A Oklahoma City.
El novato Josue De Paula fue enviado de vuelta a ligas menores; podría regresar para la postemporada
Con el regreso de Ohtani, Josue De Paula bajó a la Triple-A para unirse a los Comets en los playoffs de la Pacific Coast League contra los Las Vegas Aviators. De Paula había estado en la alineación como bateador designado.
De Paula se convirtió rápidamente en un favorito de los aficionados durante la ausencia de Ohtani. El neoyorquino de 21 años se embasó de manera segura en 10 de sus primeros 11 juegos en las Grandes Ligas. Se fue de 3-2 con una carrera anotada y una base por bolas, mientras conseguía el primer triple de su carrera en la victoria de los Dodgers por 7-0 sobre los Padres el martes.
___

The two-way superstar has been on the IL since Sept. 9 due to right biceps inflammation and lingering soreness in his left knee. item.content:encoded:
Dodgers’ Ohtani set for return Wednesday after IL stint; Roberts says he’s ‘considerably’ better
LOS ANGELES (AP) — Shohei Ohtani is expected to be back in the Los Angeles Dodgers’ lineup on Wednesday after a stint on the injured list.
The two-way superstar has been on the IL since Sept. 9 due to right biceps inflammation and lingering soreness in his left knee.
Manager Dave Roberts said Ohtani is feeling “considerably” better.
“I would say if he was a five, he’s probably an eight or a nine right now,” Roberts said Tuesday before the Dodgers faced San Diego.
The Dodgers clinched their 13th NL West title in 14 years without Ohtani, who was in Los Angeles for treatment when the team beat Cincinnati on the road last week. Now, the four-time MVP will have five games remaining to get some at-bats in before the postseason begins.
Ohtani is likely to resume his role as the Dodgers’ leadoff hitter, especially against right-handed pitching. Mookie Betts has been atop the lineup and is hitting .373 this month.
“That’s probably the way it’s going to fall out, but I haven’t totally decided yet,” Roberts said, adding that he would consider Betts’ leadoff value against left-handed pitching. “I have to think about the entire lineup structure.”

item.title: [Dodgers Nation] Dalton Rushing Factored Into Dodgers’ Josue De Paula Demotion

item.description: Los Angeles Dodgers catcher Dalton Rushing is the main reason red-hot prospect Josue De Paula was demoted. item.content:encoded:
Los Angeles Dodgers catcher Dalton Rushing is the main reason red-hot prospect Josue De Paula was demoted.
The roster battle between Rushing and De Paula
For the postseason roster, Rushing and De Paula are competing for the last bench spot as a lefty pinch-hitter.
De Paula was sent down to Triple-A for the next week, opening a spot for Shohei Ohtani on the active roster.
Later on, Rushing will be activated and get his shot at the plate.
“It’s going to be a good debate,” manager Dave Roberts said to reporters. “Hitting off the bench is very difficult, and so you’re just trying to figure out who gives us the best chance.
“We have to have those conversations and make a decision.”
By demoting De Paula now, he can be added back to the active roster in time for the postseason if the team chooses him.
Where both Rushing and De Paula currently stand
Through 11 games in the big leagues, De Paul is hitting .323/.500/.545 with a 1.081 OPS. He is getting on base during half of his plate appearances, and he is really making hitters work.
On the other hand, Rushing has been on the injured list with an elbow injury.
He came back in early September, had four pinch-hit at-bats, and then went back on the injured list after his throwing program set him back.
With such obvious momentum for De Paula, the organization still wants to give Rushing a chance, though
“To be quite frank, it’s going to be tougher for Dalton given the time that he’s missed, and … you have three games to get back in the playoff form, which is tough to do,” Roberts explained
“It’s not a knock on him. He’s been great for us. But it’s still tough given that you’re also talking about the consistency of at-bats recently from Josue.”
Unless Rushing really puts something great together, Roberts and the Dodgers have no choice but to give De Paula a shot.
“Just showing them that I can swing it, and it’s an option,” Rushing told The LA Times after a recent batting practice.
“I know that you kind of tie [the team’s] hands up when you can’t play defense. So, I’m not expecting anything… just continue to take at-bats and see where we go from there.”

item.content:encoded:
When the Los Angeles Dodgers called up Josue De Paula just a few weeks ago, there weren’t really any major expectations for him to carry the offense or make a huge contribution this season. He was here to get his cup of coffee and gain some invaluable MLB experience. But in his short time with the club, De Paula has made such a massive impression that he has already forced a potential postseason roster battle that could end up with him on top.
As reported by Katie Woo of The Athletic, De Paula has become an unexpected yet good problem for the Dodgers as they are set to welcome back a number of players from the IL. The team activated superstar Shohei Ohtani after he had been dealing with a handful of nagging injuries.
The Dodgers will also look to activate catcher Dalton Rushing from the IL before the end of the regular season. While he will not be able to return behind the plate this year, the team could potentially use his bat off of the bench. This could lead to a log jam on the bench and a position battle between Rushing and De Paula ... down the line. To begin the proceedings, De Paula will go down on Wednesday in favor of Ohtani, while Rushing till ideally get some at-bats at the MLB level before the season ends.
This doesn't mean De Paula can be counted out of the postseason roster mix, though. That debate hasn't finished yet (or even begun until Rushing can get some reps).
While Dodgers manager Dave Roberts admitted earlier in the week that it could lead to a “good debate” as the team determines which of the two players to carry on the postseason roster, he may have already shown his hand.
“To be quite frank, it’s going to be tougher for Dalton, given the time that he’s missed, and to kind of think that you have three games to get back in playoff form, which is tough to do,” Roberts said of Rushing.
“It’s not a knock on him. He’s been great for us. But it’s still tough, given that also you’re talking about the consistency of at-bats recently from Josue. We have to have those conversations and make a decision.”
With just a handful of games remaining in the regular season, Rushing likely won’t get many at-bats to get back into a rhythm before the playoffs. Whether or not that will have the greatest impact on Roberts’ final decision will be interesting to watch out for. It will be hard to overlook how hot De Paula is at the plate right now though, even as he heads to the minors.
Josue De Paula has already become a force in the Dodgers’ lineup
Through his first 31 at-bats with the Dodgers, De Paula has already collected 10 hits and driven in seven runs. With a .323/.500/.581 slash line, he has shown that he’s capable of handling MLB pitching. Well, at least in the short term. We have seen rookies come up to the majors and wreak havoc at the plate before teams have time to collect enough tape on them and pitchers can make the adjustment.
Then again, as the Dodgers' No. 1 prospect, De Paula has raked at every level in the minor leagues. With a career .857 OPS in five minor league seasons, he has the tools to make the adjustments of his own. He already has an excellent grasp on the strike zone and plate discipline that rivals seasoned MLB veterans. De Paula has drawn 11 walks in 11 games in his young career in the bigs.
The postseason is obviously a different beast than a prospect’s first dozen MLB games. At-bats are more scrutinized and the pressure would be unlike anything De Paula has experienced in his pro career. He also lacks the experience of coming off the bench cold and pinch hitting, especially in high-leverage situations. But if anyone could overcome those obstacles, it is De Paula.
Despite Roberts already seeming to have a preference, De Paula isn’t a lock for the playoff roster quite yet. But with the ability to change the game with one swing, he could become one of the Dodgers’ most dangerous weapons off the bench in October.

item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES — The Dodgers on Wednesday activated Shohei Ohtani off the injured list on his first day eligible to return after the minimum 15 days on the sideline with right biceps inflammation. Josue De Paula was optioned to Triple-A Oklahoma City.
The plan is for Ohtani to be the designated hitter for the remaining five games of the regular season, to get him back in the swing of things at the plate. An accumulation of injuries ate into a very productive season for the four-time MVP. Left knee inflammation prevented Ohtani from pitching after July 3, and the right biceps injury started showing signs at the plate as well.
Ohtani last homered on August 18, part of a stretch of three home runs in two days at Coors Field. On that date, Ohtani was hitting .294/.390/.558 with a 153 wRC+, leading the National League in slugging percentage and OPS, and a close second to Pete Crow-Armstrong (155) in wRC+.
But in 13 games since, Ohtani had just six hits in 49 at-bats (.122/.295/.184) with 21 strikeouts and 10 walks. The Dodgers tried avoiding the IL, giving Ohtani four days off before returning on September 7, when he was hitless in three at-bats plus a walk, but aggravated the right biceps injury on a swing. That was the last straw that finally landed Ohtani on the injured list for extended rest.
“When he’s activated, he’s going to be in the best physical place he’s been in quite some time,” manager Dave Roberts said over the weekend, than on Tuesday added, “I would say if he was a five, he’s probably an eight or nine right now.”
Ohtani on the shelf opened a door for De Paula, the Dodgers’ top prospect, to get called up directly from Double-A. The Dodgers were hesitant to give De Paula playing time in the corner outfield, sticking with Teoscar Hernández and Kyle Tucker, who have each thrived in September. But with designated hitter open, De Paula had a chance to play every day, and he seized the opportunity.
De Paula has reached base in half of his 42 plate appearances, hitting .323/.500/.581 with three doubles, a triple, and a home run in his 11 games, and he has 11 walks against only five strikeouts.
“I think Josue has done a fantastic job,” Roberts said Tuesday.
Sending De Paula down to the minors means he won’t play in any of the Dodgers’ final five regular season games, but it doesn’t prevent him from making the postseason roster. De Paula needs to be on optional assignment for at least 10 days, a clock that does not stop for teams in the postseason. Getting sent down on Wednesday means his first day eligible to return is Saturday, October 3, which is the day of Game 1 of the National League Division Series.
He’s in a battle with Dalton Rushing for the left-handed bat off the bench, and De Paula has the built-in advantages that Rushing can’t really play in the field with the partially torn UCL in his right elbow, and that Rushing has been sidelined for two and a half weeks on the injured list.
“To be quite frank, it’s going to be tougher for Dalton given the time he’s missed, and to think that you have [three] games to get back into playoff form, it’s tough to do,” Roberts said Tuesday. “It’s not a knock on him, he’s been great for us, but it’s still tough, right, Given that we talk about having the consistency of at-bats recently from Josue. But we have to have those conversations and make a decision.”

item.title: [Yahoo] Shohei Ohtani tiene previsto regresar el miércoles, pero los Dodgers aún tienen dudas por resolver
item.dc:creator: Maddie Lee
item.description: A los Dodgers les queda menos de una semana de la temporada regular para ponerse en forma para los playoffs. item.content:encoded:
A los Dodgers les queda menos de una semana de la temporada regular para ponerse en forma para los playoffs. Y los movimientos en su plantilla para esta serie reflejan esa prisa por el tiempo.
El mánager Dave Roberts confirmó el martes que Shohei Ohtani (bíceps derecho, rodilla izquierda) iba a ser reincorporado el miércoles tras su estancia de 15 días en la lista de lesionados. Según Roberts, Ohtani se siente "considerablemente" mejor que antes de estar en la lista de lesionados.
"Diría que si antes estaba en un nivel de cinco, ahora probablemente esté en un ocho o un nueve", dijo Roberts antes de que ocho lanzadores lideraran la victoria de los Dodgers por 7-0 contra los Padres de San Diego en el primer partido de la serie.
El martes, los Dodgers redujeron a uno su número mágico para asegurar una exención en la primera ronda. Y antes del partido, recuperaron a otros dos jugadores importantes para la postemporada, al reincorporar del lista de lesionados al jardinero central Andy Pages (fractura en la mano izquierda) y al lanzador derecho Roki Sasaki (ampolla en el dedo medio derecho).
En movimientos correspondientes, los Dodgers enviaron al equipo de Triple A de Oklahoma City al lanzador derecho Emmet Sheehan y al receptor Eliézer Alfonzo.
Sasaki se hizo cargo de la cuarta entrada del partido con relevos y lanzó sin permitir carreras. Permitió un par de sencillos, pero su bola rápida tuvo un poco más de vida en esa breve participación, con un promedio de 98.7 mph y una velocidad máxima de 101.7.
"Pude adaptarme porque ya tenía la experiencia [desde el bullpen] del año pasado", dijo Sasaki a través del intérprete Kensuke Okubo. "Probablemente voy a lanzar en un par de partidos más, así que solo voy a hacer ajustes y seguir avanzando".
Pages se fue de 0 de 2, pero llegó a base dos veces, gracias a un golpeado por lanzamiento y una base por bolas.
"Obviamente, al haber estado fuera un mes, no me siento del todo bien ni tan cómodo al bate", dijo Pages a través del intérprete del equipo, Juan Dorado. "Pero hay cosas [de batear con la máquina Trajekt] que me ayudaron a poder regresar".
Sin embargo, incluso con el regreso de los jugadores, aún hay preguntas que los Dodgers deben responder en la última semana de la temporada:
¿En qué posición bateará Ohtani?
Al menos al principio, Roberts planea colocar a Ohtani al inicio del orden de bateo, como de costumbre. Pero el campocorto Mookie Betts ha entrado en la discusión.
"Sin duda, contra lanzadores diestros [Ohtani] estará ahí", dijo Roberts. "Creo que debería analizar la situación de Mookie contra lanzadores zurdos, pero tengo que pensar en la estructura completa de la alineación".
Ohtani ha sido el primer bateador en todos los partidos que ha sido titular este año. Pero bateó en el segundo lugar en 79 partidos entre las dos temporadas anteriores combinadas.
Incluso sin Ohtani, la alineación de los Dodgers ha estado funcionando bien. El martes, Tommy Edman conectó su segundo jonrón en otros tantos partidos, y Will Smith conectó un jonrón por tercera vez en cuatro días.
¿Está sana la rotación?
El lanzador zurdo de los Dodgers, Blake Snell, quien salió de su apertura la semana pasada por una contractura en la ingle izquierda, realizó una sesión de bullpen el martes. Está programado para una última apertura en la temporada regular el sábado, dijo Roberts.
Eso significa que los cuatro abridores proyectados de los Dodgers para los playoffs están programados para lanzar de este miércoles a sábado, con Yoshinobu Yamamoto y Tyler Glasnow en el montículo para los dos últimos partidos contra los Padres, y Tarik Skubal y Snell en los dos primeros partidos en San Francisco.
¿Quién es el cerrador?
En resumen, podría cambiar de un día para otro.
"En un mundo perfecto —aunque todos sabemos que el mundo no es perfecto—, me encantaría tener [un cerrador fijo]", dijo Roberts. "Creo que si surge la oportunidad, por ejemplo, de que Tanner [Scott] lance una entrada decisiva en la séptima u octava entrada, es difícil dejar pasar esa oportunidad si él es la mejor opción en ese momento. Porque simplemente no sabes cómo se desarrollará la novena entrada.
"Esas son cosas con las que hay que lidiar, y siempre es bueno que la gente las discuta. En este momento no veo a un cerrador que sea solo una persona".
Sasaki asumió ese papel el año pasado. No está claro exactamente cómo lo utilizará Roberts esta vez, pero Roberts dijo que podría ser una opción, dependiendo de cómo lance al regresar de la lista de lesionados.
"El año pasado fue una de esas situaciones de necesidad, dada nuestra situación en cuanto al rendimiento, la salud y la plantilla", dijo Roberts. "Desempeñó ese papel de manera admirable".
El martes, fue uno de los ocho lanzadores de los Dodgers que, en conjunto, lograron una blanqueada en un día de bullpen.
"Hemos tenido mucho talento a lo largo de los años", dijo Roberts. "Pero al sentarnos aquí hoy, al final de la temporada, el bullpen está en la mejor forma en la que ha estado. Eso podría cambiar en un día, en un partido, como todos sabemos. Pero en este momento, me siento muy bien con todos los que están ahí afuera".
El lanzador derecho Edwin Díaz, quien perdió el puesto de cerrador debido a una combinación de lesiones y bajo rendimiento, está en camino de volver a ser considerado para la novena entrada. El martes, retiró a los primeros bateadores de la alineación en orden para una quinta entrada limpia, lo que marcó su tercera salida consecutiva sin permitir carreras desde que regresó de la lista de lesionados.
"Si eres uno de los 12 o 13 lanzadores en una posible lista para la postemporada, estás en la lista de los que gozan de confianza", dijo Roberts. "Y él se ha colocado justo en medio de esa conversación. Y considerando todo lo que ha tenido que pasar este año para enderezar el rumbo, es un gran mérito para él".
¿Quién se queda con el último lugar en la banca?
La contienda por ser el bateador zurdo de la banca en la postemporada se ha reducido al novato Josué De Paula y al receptor lesionado Dalton Rushing (distensión en el flexor derecho). Pero con Rushing aún en la lista de lesionados, De Paula parece tener ventaja.
No le des demasiada importancia al movimiento correspondiente de los Dodgers con respecto a Ohtani el miércoles. Si envían a De Paula a las ligas menores a 10 días del primer partido de la Serie Divisional de la Liga Nacional, aún puede ser incluido en la plantilla.
Los Dodgers tendrán que hacer otro movimiento en la plantilla más adelante en la semana, cuando planean activar a Rushing. Si envían a un jugador a las ligas menores para hacerle espacio a Rushing, ese jugador solo sería elegible para el inicio de la Serie Divisional de la Liga Nacional como transacción correspondiente a un movimiento a la lista de lesionados.

Dave Roberts y los Dodgers viven una jornada especial ya que, finalmente, podrían asegurar ser uno de los dos mejores campeones divisionales en la Liga Nacional y evitar jugar la Serie de Comodines; todo esto ante unos Padres que, pese a una buena racha, necesitan ganar urgentemente para no rezagarse en la carrera por los puestos de playoffs.
¿Cómo llegan al juego Dodgers y Padres HOY?
Los Angeles Dodgers están teniendo un gran cierre de temporada llegando a esta jornada con 5 juegos ganados en fila, el más reciente blanqueando a los Padres por 7-0 durante un juego de bullpen. El de hoy representa un día especial para los Dodgers por el regreso de Shohei Ohtani de la lista de lesionados; el manager aseguró que está “significativamente mejor” tras presentar molestias en la rodilla izquierda y el bíceps derecho.
A shutdown performance from the 'pen. ???? pic.twitter.com/JPJbMfqkWO

According to Roberts, Diaz has shown enough to be in the conversation for high-leverage relief spots, and possibly even a save opportunity. “I think it’s one of those things that if you’re one of the 12, 13 pitchers on a potential postseason roster, you’re in the trust tree,” Roberts said. “And he’s put himself r
item.content:encoded:
Los Angeles Dodgers manager Dave Roberts made a massive statement in support of Edwin Diaz, the reliever who has long struggled but has found some form recently.
Edwin Diaz, the closer?
According to Roberts, Diaz has shown enough to be in the conversation for high-leverage relief spots, and possibly even a save opportunity.
“I think it’s one of those things that if you’re one of the 12, 13 pitchers on a potential postseason roster, you’re in the trust tree,” Roberts said.
“And he’s put himself right smack in that conversation. Given all that he’s had to go through this year to right the ship, it’s a big credit to him.”
As for his usage, Roberts could deploy Diaz in a possible save opportunity over his next two relief appearances.
The Dodgers enter Wednesday with five games left, and according to Roberts, Diaz will pitch in two, with one possibly coming in the ninth.
“The way he’s throwing the ninth is possible,” Roberts highlighted.
How has Edwin Diaz pitched recently?
Edwin Diaz returned from the injured list on September 18th against the San Francisco Giants, where he was put into low-leverage spots at first.
He threw a scoreless outing, allowing just one hit and getting two punchouts. Then, he had another scoreless outing the following day, allowing a walk and getting two strikeouts.
Finally, against the San Diego Padres, he got two strikeouts in yet another shutout inning.
In total, he has pitched three innings, with six strikeouts, no runs, one hit, and a walk.
Even more important for Diaz, he has allowed no hard-hit balls or barrels. He has thrown 40 strikes over 60 pitches.
His fastball has life, while his slider has more movement. More importantly, Diaz’s command is better than ever, allowing him to pinpoint pitches and avoid giving up too many walks.
If he keeps this up and his confidence grows, Diaz has the pedigree and experience to be a serious postseason asset, possibly as the closer.

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] “Take Pressure Off Shohei Ohtani” – MLB Analyst Explains What Dodgers Should Do With Mookie Betts Once Injured DH Returns
item.dc:creator: Krutik Jain
item.description: The Los Angeles Dodgers' leadoff spot could be a toss-up between Mookie Betts and Shohei Ohtani come postseason. While Ohtani has done an exceptional job at the top for most of the season, his latest injury concerns and a drop in performance lately have made an MLB analyst wonder if the Dodgers should consider giving the job to Betts in October. item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers' leadoff spot could be a toss-up between Mookie Betts and Shohei Ohtani come postseason. While Ohtani has done an exceptional job at the top for most of the season, his latest injury concerns and a drop in performance lately have made an MLB analyst wonder if the Dodgers should consider giving the job to Betts in October.
Betts is having a great month in September, batting .373/.468/.746 with six home runs, and posting a 1.215 OPS, 227 wRC+, and 1.6 fWAR. Betts' stellar hitting and previous success at the leadoff spot have former MLB player Xavier Scruggs convinced the Dodgers need to make the move and take the pressure off Ohtani.
"It takes pressure off Ohtani, putting him in the two-spot," Scruggs said of Betts. "And I think it's a real decision for Dave Roberts because, look, before Ohtani went on the IL, and it's almost like you don't know exactly what to expect once he comes back. So maybe that's a situation where, since his numbers have dropped, we ease it on him."
Ohtani's numbers were really off in the last 13 games before he hit the injured list. The Dodgers star batted just .122/.295/.184 with just one extra-base hit and struck out 21 times.
The contrast in performance could give Dodgers manager Dave Roberts a small headache before finalizing his postseason lineup.
When Can Dodgers Expect Shohei Ohtani to Return?
Shohei Ohtani will return to the Dodgers lineup on Wednesday against the San Diego Padres. Manager Dave Roberts confirmed he is ready to be reinstated from the 15-day injured list.
Ohtani will return as designated hitter, as he has already been shut down as a pitcher for the remainder of the season. The Dodgers superstar was suffering from right biceps inflammation and lingering left knee soreness, prompting his move to the injured list.
Ohtani is expected to resume hitting at the top of the lineup, though there are discussions about whether he could play behind Mookie Betts against left-handed pitching.
"That's probably the way it's going to fall out, but I haven't totally decided yet," Roberts said. "I have to think about the entire lineup structure."
The Dodgers have already clinched the NL West title and are strongly putting their foot forward to complete a World Series three-peat. Ohtani's return just before the postseason is to ensure the Japanese star gets some game time and finds his form at the plate.

item.title: [newsonjapan.com] Asian Games Day 5 Brings Swimming Gold and Gymnastics Drama
item.description: NAGOYA - Japan's Asian Games campaign produced another day of records and medals on September 23, with Shoon Mitsunaga setting a national record to win the men's 100-meter butterfly, both Japanese gymnastics teams taking silver behind China, and Toshikazu Yamanishi adding to the host nation's athletics medal haul.
