item.content:encoded:
NAGOYA - Japan's Asian Games campaign produced another day of records and medals on September 23, with Shoon Mitsunaga setting a national record to win the men's 100-meter butterfly, both Japanese gymnastics teams taking silver behind China, and Toshikazu Yamanishi adding to the host nation's athletics medal haul.
Away from the Games, the professional baseball pennant races entered their final stages, with Hanshin fighting to retain its Central League lead and SoftBank approaching the Pacific League championship.
The fifth day of the Asian Games brought a particularly intense contest between Japan and China, whose athletes met in swimming, gymnastics and athletics. China's 13-year-old swimming sensation Yu Zidi completed a remarkable hat trick of individual gold medals, while its men's and women's gymnastics teams narrowly defeated Japan in front of home spectators.
Japan's September 23 sporting program extended well beyond the principal medal events, with competition across rowing, fencing, table tennis, shooting, cycling, combat sports and a wide range of other disciplines. The Asian Games will continue through October 4, with athletics beginning its seven-day program in Nagoya.
Japan's swimming successes were led by 21-year-old Mitsunaga, who won the men's 100-meter butterfly at Tokyo Aquatics Centre in 50.56 seconds, lowering the Japanese record from 50.81. Defending champion Katsuo Matsumoto also reached the podium, taking bronze and giving Japan two medals in the event.
The result was particularly striking given Mitsunaga's performance in the morning heats, when he qualified seventh in 52.54 seconds. His improvement in the final brought Japan its second successive Asian Games gold in the event.
Japan added three silver medals and another bronze in the pool. Rio Shirai finished second in the women's 100-meter backstroke, while 35-year-old Satomi Suzuki collected silver in the women's 100-meter breaststroke in a Games-record time of 1:05.83. Komi Kato took bronze in the same event, and Japan's mixed 4x100-meter medley relay team finished second. Suzuki's result was her 11th career Asian Games medal.
China's Yu Zidi provided the day's other major swimming story. The 13-year-old won the women's 400-meter individual medley in 4:28.56, setting a Games record and completing three victories in three individual events after earlier winning the 200-meter butterfly and 200-meter individual medley.
China also won the men's 200-meter freestyle through Zhang Zhanshuo and the women's 100-meter backstroke through Peng Xuwei.
Japan's gymnastics teams experienced remarkably similar outcomes in their two team finals, finishing second to China in both competitions.
In the men's final, China scored 259.095 points, finishing just over one point ahead of the Japanese team. Zhang Boheng secured the title with a strong horizontal bar routine after Japan had entered the final rotation with a chance to overturn China's lead.
Olympic champion Shinnosuke Oka, competing with a back injury, fell during his horizontal bar routine and received 12.966. Teammate Daiki Hashimoto produced strong performances on pommel horse and vault, but China retained the Asian Games team title for a third consecutive edition.
Japan also took silver in the women's competition, scoring 165.362 points against China's 166.462. The Japanese team comprised Aiko Sugihara, Rina Kishi, Misa Nishiyama, Mana Okamura and Haruka Nakamura. It was Japan's ninth successive Asian Games medal in the women's team event.
The results followed Sugihara's individual all-around gold on September 22, the first by a Japanese woman at the Asian Games. The women's team will now turn its attention to the world championships in the Netherlands in October.
Soft tennis supplied two more gold medals for Japan. Toshiki Uematsu won the men's singles title, with fellow Japanese player Takuya Kurosaka taking silver, while Reina Tenma captured the women's singles championship.
Japan also secured medals across several less-publicized sports. Nanoka Kida took silver in the women's jianshu and qiangshu combined event in wushu. The equestrian eventing team earned silver, with Olympic veteran Yoshiaki Oiwa adding an individual bronze, while cyclist Yudai Todome finished third in the men's road race.
Athletics opened its program with the men's and women's half-marathon race walks. Japan's two-time world champion Toshikazu Yamanishi finished second in the men's competition behind China's Shi Shengji, who broke away after the 10-kilometer mark. China also won the women's race through Yang Liujing.
The athletics program, running through September 29 at Mizuho Park in Nagoya, will bring further Japanese contenders into action as track and field joins swimming, gymnastics and other established medal-producing sports.
Japan's team-sport campaigns also advanced significantly on September 23. The men's under-21 soccer team defeated Thailand 3-0 at Toyota Stadium to complete the group stage with three victories and no goals conceded. Yotaro Nakajima opened the scoring in the 31st minute before Keita Kosugi and Hisatsugu Ishii added two goals in quick succession early in the second half.
Japan had previously beaten Hong Kong 2-0 and Kyrgyzstan 7-0. The victory over Thailand secured first place in Group A and set up a September 26 quarterfinal against North Korea, which qualified from Group B after defeating Iran 4-1. Japan is seeking its first men's Asian Games soccer title since 2010.
The women's table tennis team also reached the final, defeating South Korea 3-0 in its semifinal at Sky Hall Toyota. Hina Hayata and Miwa Harimoto were among the players who helped Japan advance to a second consecutive Asian Games team final. Japan will face defending champion China on September 24, seeking its first women's team gold since the 1966 Bangkok Games.
Asian Games baseball produced another emphatic Japanese result as the corporate-league national team defeated the Philippines 7-0 at Toyohashi Municipal Stadium.
Japan scored twice in the second inning and three times in the third before adding another two runs in the sixth. Koya Yano and Masami Soeda each hit a two-run home run, while starting pitcher Kenta Nagano and reliever Kato combined to hold the Philippines to three hits. Japan completed its opening-round campaign unbeaten after earlier defeating China 11-3 and Palestine 15-0.
The three victories gave Japan first place in Group A and a place in the Super Round on September 25 and 26. The medal games are scheduled for September 27. Japan is attempting to win its first Asian Games baseball gold since 1994.
Japan's rowing team also reached an important milestone, with all 10 of its entered boats qualifying for their respective A finals despite heavy rain forcing changes to the competition schedule at the Nagaragawa International Regatta Course in Gifu Prefecture. The medal races are scheduled for September 24.
Outside the Asian Games, Hanshin strengthened its position at the top of the Central League with an 8-4 victory over Yakult at Jingu Stadium, extending its winning streak to four games.
Haruto Takahashi pitched six innings, allowing one run on five hits to record his league-leading 15th victory. Thirteen of those wins have come away from home, making him the first Hanshin pitcher to achieve that mark since Minoru Murayama in 1965.
The result was particularly important after the Tigers entered the day with a 1.5-game advantage over Yomiuri and a championship magic number of eight. The Giants remained in contention with a 2-1 victory over Hiroshima at Mazda Stadium.
SoftBank also moved closer to the Pacific League title, defeating Seibu 10-3 at Mizuho PayPay Dome in Fukuoka. The Hawks' latest victory came as Nippon-Ham lost 5-3 to Rakuten at Es Con Field Hokkaido. Orix defeated Lotte 1-0 at ZOZO Marine Stadium, with Ryoma Ikeda hitting his first career home run to provide the game's only run.
The day's other Central League result was a 4-3 victory for DeNA over Chunichi at Yokohama Stadium.
Soccer's domestic cup competition added another dimension to the day's schedule, with the Emperor's Cup continuing on September 23. All six J1 clubs facing J2 opposition advanced, including Kashima Antlers, for whom 18-year-old Minato Yoshida scored his first goal. Kashiwa Reysol also progressed with a victory over FC Imabari.
Grand sumo's September tournament reached its 11th day at Ryogoku Kokugikan, where yokozuna Onosato strengthened his position at the top of the championship race with a victory over sekiwake Fujinokawa. Onosato improved to 10 wins and one defeat, opening a two-victory advantage after all three wrestlers who had entered the day with two losses were beaten.
Ozeki Aonishiki defeated Takanosho to secure his eighth victory and a winning record. Sekiwake Atamifuji suffered his third defeat against ozeki Kirishima, while former ozeki Asanoyama improved to 8-3 with a victory over Kinbozan. With four days remaining, Onosato led a group of six wrestlers on three losses.
In Major League Baseball, attention surrounding Shohei Ohtani shifted toward his expected return to the Los Angeles Dodgers lineup after a spell on the injured list. Manager Dave Roberts confirmed on September 22 that Ohtani was scheduled to be reinstated on September 23 following treatment for knee and biceps problems. The Dodgers had already secured the National League West title and were preparing for the postseason.
Japan's September 23 sports program illustrated the breadth of the country's increasingly crowded autumn calendar, from national-record swimming performances and Asian Games medals to domestic baseball pennant races, international soccer, professional sumo and Japanese athletes competing overseas.
The next day of Asian Games competition will bring Japan's women's table tennis team into its final against China, rowing's medal races and the opening apparatus finals in artistic gymnastics, with further opportunities for the host nation to add to its medal total.

item.title: [Sports Illustrated] Josue De Paula or Dalton Rushing? Dodgers Weighing Difficult Postseason Decision
item.dc:creator: Gabe Smallson; Unknown
item.description: The Los Angeles Dodgers are looking to do what no Major League Baseball team has done in the last quarter-century and win three consecutive championships. Despite all the talent on the roster, each name on the 26-man roster come postseason will have more importance than the next. Even someone like Miguel Rojas — who was hitless for a calendar month heading into the World Series — can come up big in perhaps the biggest moment in the history of the sport. All of this not only boils down to how the
item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers are looking to do what no Major League Baseball team has done in the last quarter-century and win three consecutive championships.
Despite all the talent on the roster, each name on the 26-man roster come postseason will have more importance than the next. Even someone like Miguel Rojas — who was hitless for a calendar month heading into the World Series — can come up big in perhaps the biggest moment in the history of the sport.
All of this not only boils down to how the two-time defending champions will perform, but who manager Dave Roberts names on the final rendition of the postseason rosters. As entertaining as the impending decision will be for onlookers of the baseball world, the skipper knows the importance of his roster choice as well as anyone.
Josue De Paula and Dalton Rushing appear to be fighting for the same thing come October, but De Paula is still a raw product and Rushing is still on the injured list with elbow discomfort.
“It’s going to be a good debate,” manager Dave Roberts said on Tuesday.
De Paula, the 21-year-old rookie from Brooklyn, NY, put up undeniable numbers in Double-A this season, leading to the outfielder's promotion before registering a single Triple-A at-bat. In his first 11 games in the big leagues, he's hitting .323/.500/.581 with a 1.081 OPS.
Rushing, on the other hand, has plenty more big league experience than De Paula since his promotion last May. Before his first IL stint, Rushing was hitting .253 with an OPS of .809 this season.
The reason for his stint on the shelf was due to a slight tear in his ulnar collateral ligament. After he returned for just four hitless games, he once again hit the injured list, but this time, MRIs gave reason to believe that the flexor tendon was the real issue, something that could potentially be addressed without surgery and assisted through platelet-rich plasma injections.
For either player, this will be an uphill battle. Roberts admitted that for Rushing specifically, it may be just a steeper incline.
“Hitting off the bench is very difficult and so you're just trying to figure out who gives us the best chance," Roberts said. “To be quite frank, it’s going to be tougher for Dalton given the time that he’s missed, and to kind of think that you have three games to get back in the playoff form, which is tough to do. It’s not a knock on him. He’s been great for us. but it’s still tough given that also you’re talking about the consistency of at-bats recently from Josue.
“We have to have those conversations and make a decision.”

Gabe Smallson is a sportswriter based in Los Angeles with a focus in sports and entertainment content. Gabe has previously worked at Newsweek and Dodgers Nation. He graduated from San Francisco State University in 2020 and received his Masters of Science at the University of Southern California in 2025.

item.title: [Dodger Blue] Dodgers manager discusses intriguing postseason roster battle
item.dc:creator: Matt Borelli
item.description: Since being called up from Double-A Tulsa earlier this month as the corresponding move for Shohei Ohtani going on the 15-day injured list, Josue De Paula has done nothing but impress his Los Angeles Dodgers teammates and coaching staff. The top prospect has flashed his elite offensive potential, showing remarkable plate discipline and power while drawing comparisons to New York Mets slugger Juan Soto. With Ohtani returning from the IL on Wednesday, questions remain about De Paula’s role with the
item.content:encoded:
Since being called up from Double-A Tulsa earlier this month as the corresponding move for Shohei Ohtani going on the 15-day injured list, Josue De Paula has done nothing but impress his Los Angeles Dodgers teammates and coaching staff.
The top prospect has flashed his elite offensive potential, showing remarkable plate discipline and power while drawing comparisons to New York Mets slugger Juan Soto.
With Ohtani returning from the IL on Wednesday, questions remain about De Paula’s role with the Dodgers moving forward. But the expectation is that he will compete with Dalton Rushing for the final spot on the team’s postseason roster.
“He’s done a great job,” manager Dave Roberts said of De Paula. “We made the move with Eliezer Alfonzo out on option with Andy (Pages) coming back. With Shohei coming back, I’m just not sure what the counter is going to be. But to your question, Josue has done a fantastic job.”
Rushing has been on the 10-day injured list since Sept. 6 after re-aggravating his right elbow while playing catch. However, he took live batting practice against Will Klein on Tuesday and should be activated in the coming days.
That would give Rushing only a few games to show the Dodgers he is back up to game speed and deserving of a spot on their postseason roster.
“Dalton, taking his at-bats. The thought is to give him an opportunity at some point in time to get activated and see how it looks coming off the bench,” Roberts said. “So I’m not sure if that’s tomorrow, Thursday, Friday, something like that.”
Rushing was in the midst of a breakout season before the right elbow injury threw him off course, so it will be interesting to see which direction the Dodgers decide to take.
Dodgers postseason roster battle
The Dodgers will consider several factors when choosing between De Paula and Rushing for the final spot on their postseason roster, including the ability to put together a good at-bat, not chasing pitches out of the strike zone and power.
“Quality of at-bat, conducting an at-bat, the ability to swing at strikes, take balls, get on base, get a hit,” Roberts explained. “There’s potential slug with both those guys. It’s going to be a good debate.
“I think hitting off the bench is very difficult, and you’re just trying to figure out who gives us the best chance. To be quite frank, it’s going to be tougher for Dalton given the time that he’s missed. To kind of think that you have three games to get back into playoff form, it’s tough to do. It’s not a knock on him. He’s been great for us, but it’s still tough.
“And also when you’re talking about having the consistency of at-bats recently from Josue. But again, we have to have those conversations and make a decision.”

item.title: [True Blue LA] Sidelined last year, Evan Phillips & Brock Stewart are ready for October
item.dc:creator: Eric Stephen

item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES — Last year at this time, Evan Phillips and Brock Stewart were both recovering from surgeries and unavailable to pitch. They were around the team but unable to contribute during the stretch run and postseason. This year, both veteran right-handers are two key cogs in an increasingly deep Dodgers bullpen and an important part of their October puzzle.
Phillips had Tommy John surgery in June 2025, wiping out the last half of last season and the first half of this one. When he returned from the injured list in July, the Dodgers were cautious in his usage, not using him on back-to-back days for his first four weeks, and used him on one day rest only four times during that stretch.
The results were spotty at first, allowing runs in five of his first seven appearances, including an uncharacteristic four home runs in such a short span. Since then, Phillips has allowed runs in only three of his last 21 appearances, and the lone home run surrendered was last Monday to Elly De La Cruz, which seems to be a rite of passage for everybody these days.
“Evan as you would expect, the first handful of outings were inconsistent coming off Tommy John, but I’d say the last [few] have been kind of who he is, and it’s been fun to see,” manager Dave Roberts said recently. “There’s a two-seamer, there’s a four-seamer, and some sweepers getting some awkward swings, some chase. That’s been good, and his command has been a lot better, too.”
Phillips in his 28 games has 28 strikeouts against only three unintentional walks. Since the start of August, the Dodgers have used Phillips more aggressively, pitching on back-to-back days five times, and he pitched three times in four days in three different stretches, and during that span has a 2.30 ERA and 2.46 FIP.
“I appreciate what they’ve done, trying to build me up, plus also protect me, plus giving me advantageous lanes while also challenging me,” Phillips said. “It’s been great so far, and I definitely feel like I’m coming closer and closer to that best version of myself that I have been and continue to strive to be.”
Stewart, a sixth-round draft pick of the Dodgers in 2014, was reacquired by the team at the 2025 trade deadline, but he pitched in only four games for them before succumbing to right shoulder debridement surgery in September. This year the right-hander has a 2.45 ERA and 2.53 xERA in his 27 games, with 24 strikeouts and seven unintentional walks in 25 2/3 innings, including a scoreless first inning to start Tuesday night’s bullpen-game shutout of the San Diego Padres.
“When Brock’s healthy, he’s as good as anyone we have,” Roberts said Tuesday. “For us, it’s just trying to manage him the right way and keep him strong and healthy. He’s been great.”
“That’s very cool to hear. I just go out there and throw it, that’s literally all I focus on. But people tell me that my — you know, I throw five pitches, which helps as a reliever,” Stewart said. “They tell me my stuff is pretty good, and it’s always nice to hear that. But I don’t know, I just go out there and throw it, try to compete as best I can, and hope it works out.
Roberts wasn’t wrong. Since returning to the majors in 2023 with the Minnesota Twins, Stewart has a 2.45 ERA and 2.78 xERA, which ranks 10th and ninth, respectively, among the 576 major league pitchers with at least 100 innings over the last four years. Tarik Skubal, with two Cy Young Awards during that stretch, has a 2.50 ERA and 2.73 xERA, for example.
But staying on the field has been a problem for Stewart, who this season alone has been on the injured list three different times — recovering from shoulder surgery, bone spur in his left foot, and shoulder discomfort — inactive for a total of 95 games. Since 2023, Stewart has also been on the injured list with elbow soreness, shoulder tendinitis, a shoulder strain, a hamstring strain, and shoulder inflammation, limited to just 106 2/3 total innings over the last four seasons.
“I feel good, but I’ve told everybody though, one day at a time. I’ve been hurt a lot so I always try to take things one day at a time. But I’m happy with the way I feel, happy with the way I felt today,” Stewart said. “Getting close to the finish line, but happy with how I feel, happy with how the stuff is coming out. I feel like I’m in a good spot and can hopefully help out.”
Stewart has pitched in the postseason only once, in three games over two series with the Minnesota Twins in 2023. Phillips was an October stalwart for the Dodgers since he was acquired on a waiver claim in 2021. In 12 appearances for the Dodgers in the playoffs, Phillips has yet to allow a run, over 15 1/3 innings, with 21 strikeouts and six unintentional walks. Phillips missed out on the World Series in 2024 with a right rotator cuff injury suffered during the NLCS, and was sidelined for all of last October.
“I love pitching in the postseason, I love competing with these guys. In 2024, missing out on the World Series, but I tried to dig in on the fact that I helped us get there, and played quite a large part in the Division Series and Championship Series. Obviously I want to see it all to the end, and help us carry that trophy off the field,” Philips said. “I’m just as eager as ever. Fortunate that I feel healthy at this time, and just trying to build on that, continue to chip away, and be the best I can when it matters most.”
This season, only Tanner Scott, Edwin Díaz, and Alex Vesia have a higher average-leverage index than Phillips and Stewart among Dodgers relievers. Phillips and Stewart have each saved a game this year, and Phillips has done so in the past with 46 saves with the Dodgers. Roberts said he’d feel comfortable with either Phillips or Stewart getting a save opportunity in October, along with a group that includes Tanner Scott and the just-activated Roki Sasaki.
“This year, more than any other year, I think there’s more guys we feel comfortable closing out games,” Roberts said.

item.title: [New York Post] Roki Sasaki ditches Dodgers plan with striking U-turn in prep for 3-peat quest
item.dc:creator: Dylan Hernandez
item.description: The initial plan called for Roki Sasaki to pitch an inning or two as an opener. Sasaki had other ideas. “I said I wanted to pitch out of the bullpen,” Sasaki said in Japanese. Because Sasaki will be deployed as a reliever in the playoffs, he figured he should spend the remainder of the regular season becoming reacquainted with the role. item.content:encoded:
The initial plan called for Roki Sasaki to pitch an inning or two as an opener.
Sasaki had other ideas.
“I said I wanted to pitch out of the bullpen,” Sasaki said in Japanese.
Because Sasaki will be deployed as a reliever in the playoffs, he figured he should spend the remainder of the regular season becoming reacquainted with the role.
So instead of throwing the first and second innings of the Dodgers’ 7-0 victory over the San Diego Padres on Tuesday night, Sasaki pitched the fourth.
Returning from a month-long stay on the injured list, Sasaki pitched in relief for the first time this season.
What was most memorable about his night wasn’t that he struck out two batters or threw six of his 20 pitches faster than 99 mph. Rather, what was most striking was his embrace of his move out of the Dodgers’ rotation.
Sasaki was reluctant to make the switch last year, doing so only as a last-ditch effort to salvage an otherwise disastrous rookie season. The decision made him an October hero, as the team’s lack of options made him the closer almost by default.
He returned to the rotation this year and was 5-5 with a 4.56 earned-run average through his first 23 games, all of them starts. His form improved over the course of the season, and he was 2-0 with a 3.05 ERA in seven starts after the All-Star break. But in the last of those starts, which was on Aug. 26 in Atlanta, he developed a blister on the middle finger of his pitching hand.
Starting games was a source of pride for Sasaki. When he agreed to try pitching in relief last year, he made the Dodgers promise him they would use him as a starter this season.
Sasaki didn’t require as much convincing when team officials started talking to him about a role change on the Dodgers’ recent trip to Cincinnati.
The Dodgers will use a four-man rotation in the playoffs, and they have four Cy Young Award-caliber pitchers in Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Blake Snell, Tarik Skubal and Tyler Glasnow. Sasaki could do the math. If he was going to pitch in the postseason, it would be as a reliever.
“I think it’s important to make the roster,” Sasaki said.
Something else: The Dodgers kept their word about him starting games, and Sasaki wanted to repay them.
“In the first half of the season, they used me as a starter even when I wasn’t pitching well,” he said.
Sasaki didn’t pitch more than five innings in any of his first five starts. His ERA at that point was 6.35. His fastball velocity was down and his command was non-existent.
The Dodgers would have been justified in removing him from the rotation.
They didn’t.
They could have sent him to the minor leagues.
They didn’t.
That meant something to Sasaki.
“This time,” Sasaki said, “I want to be able to contribute to the team in whatever shape.”
The feelings point to a growing trust that has developed between Sasaki and the Dodgers.
At this stage of the season last year, they didn’t seem to be on the same page. As he shined as their closer last October, Dodgers officials and coaches told stories about how they helped Sasaki rediscover his 100-mph fastball. Sasaki downplayed the team’s role in his resurgence, saying he figured out what he was doing wrong by watching videos of himself pitching in high school.
Sasaki is said to have become more open to instruction this season, which contributed to an improved fastball as well as the incorporation of a different variation of his signature forkball.
He is also physically stronger than he did last year. Fatigue was a factor for him in the postseason, and by the World Series, he looked like a spent cartridge. To close out Game 7 of the World Series, manager Dave Roberts went to Yamamoto, who was pitching his third inning in relief a day after making a six-inning start.
Sasaki looks more capable of shouldering a reliever’s schedule and workload.
Sasaki closing games in the upcoming postseason is “certainly an option,” manager Dave Roberts said.
Edwin Diaz has worked his way back into ninth-inning consideration by posting three consecutive scoreless appearances since his return from his latest IL stint. Tanner Scott has been the Dodgers’ primary closer this season, but Roberts said there could be instances in which the left-hander is used earlier in games in high-leverage situations.
Sasaki said he would pitch whenever asked.
That could be determined by how he looks over this final week of the regular season. Roberts said he will likely pitch next on Friday in San Francisco.
This time around, there isn’t any hesitation on the part of Sasaki. This time around, he really wants to do this.

item.content:encoded:
Los Angeles Dodgers pitcher Roki Sasaki directly asked manager Dave Roberts about his role upon his return.
Roki Sasaki’s request
After returning to the Dodgers and making a one-inning appearance, Sasaki spoke to reporters and revealed a hidden detail about his role upon his return.
He said he personally requested to move into a bullpen role to adjust and get used to his postseason role.
With all of the starting pitchers healthy, Sasaki will be relegated to a high-leverage postseason reliever, allowing his three pitches to shine.
Sasaki is willing to do whatever is best for the team, even if it involves not pitching as much as usual.
“I’m just going to give my best, whatever opportunity I’m given,” Sasaki said. “Doesn’t matter if it’s a couple innings or not, just go out there and perform.”
Dave Roberts celebrated Sasaki’s unselfishness and willingness to put the team before himself.
“It’s just showing that whatever it takes to help us win, knowing that any inning he throws in the postseason is going to be huge,” Roberts said. “He clearly understands that.”
How did Roki’s return from injury go?
Sasaki suffered a blister on his right middle finger, which kept him on the injured list for a couple of weeks.
The Japanese righty was activated on Tuesday, September 22nd, and after his activation, he has been put into a relief role, pitching just one inning
Sasaki came into the fourth inning, allowed two hits, and pitched a shutout inning. He also added two punchouts and threw 20 pitches.
According to Baseball Savant, he allowed just one hard hit. Sasaki allowed four whiffs on 11 different swings. Additionally, he got two called strikes.
Both of his strikeouts came on the splitter, his signature pitch. His fastball was 0.9 MPH faster than his season average.
All in all, his first taste of competitive pitching was a success, and Dave Roberts should trust him, given his exploits as the closer last year.

item.title: [heraldglobe.com] Dodgers' Shohei Ohtani to return to lineup vs. Padres
item.description:
Field Level Media

item.content:encoded:
Field Level Media

23 Sep 2026, 19:49 GMT+10

(Photo credit: Jayne Kamin)
Shohei Ohtani is expected to be back in the starting lineup Wednesday, Yoshinobu Yamamoto will be on the mound and the Los Angeles Dodgers will accelerate their playoff preparations in a home game against the San Diego Padres.
Ohtani last played Sept. 7, one day after he struck out a season-high four times, and has been on the injured list with right biceps discomfort ever since.
With five regular-season games remaining, Ohtani will get a chance to build some momentum for the postseason.
'Unless I hear otherwise, he'll be in the lineup,' said Dodgers manager Dave Roberts, who admitted that the team's leading home-run hitter with 30 is about an '8 or 9' on a health scale of 1-10.
Where to put Ohtani in the lineup is another question. Normally the Dodgers' leadoff hitter, Mookie Betts has made the top spot his own lately.
With the Padres set to start left-hander Robbie Ray, the right-handed Betts likely is to hit leadoff Wednesday, while Ohtani could be in his former No. 2 spot. Betts went 1-for-4 with an RBI and a run scored in Tuesday's 7-0 victory over the Padres and is batting .366 since the start of September.
Yamamoto (14-8, 2.51 ERA) has looked like an ace all season and has been at his best of late by going 3-1 with a 1.79 ERA over his last seven starts. The right-hander is 3-3 with a 3.76 ERA in seven career starts against San Diego.
The Dodgers (97-60) increased their home winning streak to 11 games and reduced their magic number to two for clinching a bye through the wild-card round. They also pulled within a game of the National League-leading Milwaukee Brewers (98-59).
Los Angeles center fielder Andy Pages returned from a broken hand on Tuesday and reached base twice.
'Obviously being out for a month, I'm not feeling all that great or familiar at the plate but there are things from the Trajekt (pitching machine) that helped me come back,' Pages said through a team interpreter.
The Padres' magic number for clinching a wild-card spot remained at two after Tuesday's loss.
Ray (13-8, 3.60) pitched well immediately after he was acquired from the San Francisco Giants at the trade deadline but has an 8.78 ERA over his past three starts. He is 3-2 with a 5.22 ERA in eight starts for San Diego.
In 26 career starts against the Dodgers, tied for his most against any club, Ray is 9-9 with a 3.81 ERA.
The Padres (87-70) entered Tuesday's series opener against the Dodgers with 13 victories in their previous 14 games but failed to find much offense as Los Angeles went to a bullpen game and used eight pitchers.
It was the second time since the All-Star break the Padres were held without a run.
San Diego also is expected to activate right-hander Jason Adam following a shoulder injury as he rejoins one of the major league's best bullpens. Adam is 2-2 with a 2.51 ERA in 36 relief appearances but has not pitched in a big-league game since June 29.
'Yeah, more than ready,' Adam said, according to the San Diego Union-Tribune. 'I feel 100% ready.'
Padres manager Craig Stammen was guarded with the team's plans.
'It's good to see him back pitching in his normal way,' Stammen said. 'Hopefully we'll have him activated before the season ends.'
--Field Level Media

item.content:encoded:
Los Angeles Dodgers star Shohei Ohtani will make his return to the lineup tonight (Wednesday, September 23) against the San Diego Padres. The Dodgers have activated the two-way standout from the 15-day injured list after he took time to rest his nagging knee and biceps injuries. Ohtani will serve as the designated hitter for the remainder of the regular season and playoffs, as he is currently unable to pitch.
Ohtani's return comes at a crucial time for the Dodgers, who are looking to solidify their position in the National League West. According to MLB.com, Dodgers manager Dave Roberts confirmed that Ohtani is now in a better physical state, rating him an "eight or a nine" on a scale of one to ten. Ohtani has been progressing well in his hitting, having taken 30-40 swings off a Trajekt machine, which simulates real pitchers.
Despite his recent struggles at the plate, Ohtani remains a key player for the Dodgers. Before his injuries, he recorded a .902 OPS and hit a team-leading 30 home runs. In his last 24 games before going on the injured list, Ohtani hit .198 with 34 strikeouts. ABC7 reported that Roberts plans to play Ohtani in every remaining game to help him reacclimate to major league pitching.
The Dodgers have managed to maintain a strong record in Ohtani's absence, going 13-3 in the last 16 games. As they prepare for the playoffs, Ohtani's return as a designated hitter is expected to bolster their lineup. The Dodgers are also considering roster adjustments, with outfield prospect Josue De Paula potentially being sent down to make room for Ohtani.
For tonight's game, the Dodgers will face the Padres with right-handed pitcher Yoshinobu Yamamoto on the mound. The game will be broadcast on SportsNet LA and available on the MLB app.

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Dodgers have difficult Mookie Betts decision to make
item.dc:creator: Matt Larter
item.description: One of the MLB's top teams, the Los Angeles Dodgers face an interesting lineup decision with Shohei Ohtani set to return from the injured list Wednesday. Ohtani has missed a little more than a week after being placed on the 15-day IL with a biceps issue, but Dodgers manager Dave Roberts announced Tuesday that the superstar will be activated. item.content:encoded:
One of the MLB's top teams, the Los Angeles Dodgers face an interesting lineup decision with Shohei Ohtani set to return from the injured list Wednesday.
Ohtani has missed a little more than a week after being placed on the 15-day IL with a biceps issue, but Dodgers manager Dave Roberts announced Tuesday that the superstar will be activated.
Ohtani has been the Dodgers' regular leadoff hitter throughout the season. However, his absence has given Mookie Betts an opportunity to bat first, and the veteran has taken full advantage.
Betts finding his stride
Jul 25, 2026; New York City, New York, USA; Los Angeles Dodgers shortstop Mookie Betts (50) throws out New York Mets third baseman Bo Bichette (not pictured) on a ground ball during the ninth inning at Citi Field. Mandatory Credit: Brad Penner-Imagn Images
Roberts said Tuesday that, "as of now," Ohtani will return to the leadoff spot. However, he also acknowledged that the Dodgers are considering a platoon at the top of the batting order.
Under that scenario, Ohtani would lead off against right-handed pitchers, while Betts would move into the top spot against left-handers.
There is a case for keeping Betts in the role, at least against certain matchups. Ohtani has struggled recently, batting .139/.262/.222 with two extra-base hits and no RBIs over his last nine games.
Betts, meanwhile, has been outstanding since moving to the top of the order. During Ohtani's absence, the 33-year-old went 9-for-16 with four doubles, two home runs and six RBIs across four games.
Dodgers face a tough choice
Betts has only batted leadoff in six games this season, but his recent production has made the decision more complicated for Roberts and the Dodgers.
His September numbers have been particularly impressive. Betts is hitting .373/.468/.746 with 13 extra-base hits and 20 RBIs over 17 games this month, showing the type of production the Dodgers were hoping to get from him after a difficult season.
The Dodgers have plenty of flexibility because of the depth throughout their lineup, and their record gives them some breathing room. Los Angeles enters Wednesday at 97-60, comfortably leading the National League West and sitting just one game behind the Milwaukee Brewers for the best record in the National League.
The Dodgers will face the San Diego Padres in the second game of their three-game series Wednesday, with five games remaining in the regular season. The return of Ohtani could give Los Angeles another major boost, but it also leaves Roberts with an intriguing decision at the top of his lineup.

item.content:encoded:
The Dodgers received two key reinforcements making their returns from injury on Tuesday, as both Andy Pages and Roki Sasaki played a factor into the team’s 7-0 shutout win over the San Diego Padres.
The Dodgers are preparing to get the final Infinity Stone added to their gauntlet, as two-way superstar Shohei Ohtani is expected to return from the injured list for Wednesday’s game against San Diego. Whether Ohtani will remain in the leadoff spot in the starting lineup is still up in the air, as Mookie Betts has been swinging a red-hot bat at the leadoff spot in his absence, per Sonja Chen of MLB.com.
“I do think I should think through the Mookie vs. left situation, but I have to think about the entire lineup structure,” Roberts said. “That’s probably the way it’s going to fall out, but I haven’t totally decided yet.”
Roki Sasaki made his first bullpen appearance since the 2025 World Series on Tuesday, as he logged a scoreless top of the fourth inning while allowing just one hit and striking out two.
Although Sasaki has vastly improved in the second half this season before suffering a blister to his pitching hand— 5.33 ERA in first half, 2.97 ERA in second half— the plan is to once again have him out of the bullpen for the postseason for a second consecutive year, per Chen.
“It’s just showing that whatever it takes to help us win, knowing that any inning he throws in the postseason is going to be huge,” manager Dave Roberts said. “He clearly understands that.”
Josue De Paula is making a strong case for making the postseason roster, as the 21-year-old rookie is slashing .323/.500/.581 while becoming the first Dodger rookie with at least a .500 on-base percentage over his first 11 games since Corey Seager in 2015.
De Paula has spent the bulk of his time in the big leagues serving as the designated hitter, filling the void Ohtani left behind. With Ohtani expected to return from the injured list on Wednesday, the next test for De Paula is to see how he can handle himself in the outfield defensively, per Maddie Lee of the Los Angeles Times.
“All the reports that we’ve gotten from our minor-league staff are right on cue,” Ebel said. “He’s been working, he’s bringing it right here to the major leagues. And it’s a pleasure for me, with some energy, coming out early every day — hasn’t missed. We’re working on game situations, ground balls, left, right, right at him, fly balls, shags during BP. So we’re on the right track.”

item.title: [New York Post] Dodgers leave door open to Edwin Diaz reclaiming closer’s role: ‘Certainly possible’
item.dc:creator: Jack Harris
item.description: In a perfect world, Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said, the team would like to have one set closer entering the playoffs. And by the end of Tuesday’s 7-0 win over the San Diego Padres, one unexpected name might have thrown their hat back into the ring. A week ago, the Dodgers were not certain Edwin Díaz would even be on their playoff roster, after the $69 million offseason signing lost his closer job amid an injury-plagued season marred by an ERA of nearly 12.00. In three outings since returning
item.content:encoded:
In a perfect world, Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said, the team would like to have one set closer entering the playoffs.
And by the end of Tuesday’s 7-0 win over the San Diego Padres, one unexpected name might have thrown their hat back into the ring.
A week ago, the Dodgers were not certain Edwin Díaz would even be on their playoff roster, after the $69 million offseason signing lost his closer job amid an injury-plagued season marred by an ERA of nearly 12.00.
In three outings since returning from the injured list, however, the three-time All-Star has suddenly looked like his old dominant self again.
So much so, Roberts said it remains “certainly possible” that he could factor into the Dodgers’ ninth-inning October plans.
Roberts made that claim after Díaz’s best performance yet, when he retired the top of the Padres’ batting order in order in a dominant fifth-inning sequence.
That marked the right-hander’s third scoreless appearance in a row –– a stretch that has included only one hit, one walk and six strikeouts –– and continued an unforeseen return to form triggered by a recent mechanical adjustment he made during a minor-league rehab stint.
“His last three have been fantastic with us,” Roberts said. “I wanted to see him against their better hitters, and he did a really nice job.”
Indeed, Díaz began his inning by ringing up Fernando Tatis Jr. on a front-door slider. He then fanned Dustin Harris at the end of a nine-pitch at-bat with a swing-and-miss slider. Had he used an ABS challenge, he could have punched out Manny Machado too. But he retired him all the same with a soft tapper back to the mound.
“Given all that he’s had to go through this year,” Roberts said, “to right the ship is a big credit to him.”
But will it be enough to put him back in consideration for closing duties?
Roberts made sure not to shut that door yet.
“The way he’s throwing, the ninth is possible, yes,” the manager said.
At the very least, it adds one more subplot to the final week of the Dodgers’ regular season.
The team, of course, has other closer options to consider. Tanner Scott has converted 23 of 27 save opportunities with a 2.77 ERA as Díaz’s replacement this year. Roki Sasaki has also returned to relief duties as he did at the end of last season, when he emerged as an emergency closing option during the Dodgers’ run to a second-straight World Series.
And as Roberts noted Tuesday, a closer-by-committee plan remains in play, as well.
But as the Dodgers set out for a three-peat this year, they always envisioned Díaz –– and his trademark trumpet bullpen entrance –– being a staple at the end of games.
Though he suffered a career-worst campaign, converting just seven of 11 save opportunities while missing three months with an elbow injury and another with neck inflammation, there might be time for him to reclaim his original role yet.

item.title: [USA Today] What Shohei Ohtani's impending return means for Dodgers' lineup
item.dc:creator: Andrés Soto

item.content:encoded:
What Shohei Ohtani's impending return means for Dodgers' lineup
Shohei Ohtani is expected to be activated from the injured list on Wednesday, Sept. 23, manager Dave Roberts told reporters on Tuesday, Sept. 22. If that holds true, it would mean the Los Angeles Dodgers' franchise cornerstone would have five games to ramp up before the start of the postseason.
Ohtani, who has been on the 15-day IL retroactively since Sept. 8 due to lingering issues with his right bicep and left knee, took coach pitch batting practice and went through his normal workout routine on Tuesday ahead of a 7-0 win over the San Diego Padres and according to the Dodgers skipper, he continues to check all the boxes necessary for a return.
"The thought is tomorrow," Roberts told reporters. "Unless I hear otherwise, he'll be in the lineup tomorrow."
The Dodgers have gotten hot in Ohtani's absence, posting an 8-3 record since Sept. 11 – the day he was placed on the IL – and outscoring their opponents 59-28 in that timeframe. They enter Wednesday on a five-game winning streak, have already won the NL West and their magic number to clinch a first-round bye is down to 1. Ohtani will have the opportunity to find his footing in low-stakes games to finish out the regular season. That's huge considering he did not face live pitching in his hitting progression. But what does his impending return mean for the rest of the Dodgers lineup?
Catcher Eliezer Alfonzo was optioned on Tuesday as center fielder Andy Pages made his return. Alex Freeland could be a candidate to get optioned with rookie Josue De Paula, who is in the middle of an impressive "trial run" in his first shot at the big leagues and making a serious push at making the playoff roster. If he does play in October, it would likely be as a lefty bat off the bench.
Dalton Rushing, who has been on the IL since Sept. 6 with right elbow discomfort, is also expected to be activated soon and will battle with De Paula for that spot over the final five games, though Roberts acknowledged that Rushing is at a disadvantage with a small window to show what he can do.
"It’s not a knock on him," Roberts told reporters. "He’s been great for us. but it’s still tough given that also you’re talking about the consistency of at-bats recently from Josue. We have to have those conversations and make a decision."
Whatever the decision ends up being, a red-hot Dodgers offense with Ohtani at the top of it – though Roberts has said he'd consider keeping Mookie Betts batting leadoff against lefties – suddenly makes them one of the toughest matchups this October just when they were looking like they were in their most vulnerable state just weeks ago.

item.title: [Los Angeles Times] Shohei Ohtani to return from IL Wednesday, but Dodgers still have unanswered questions in final week
item.dc:creator: Maddie Lee
item.description: Shohei Ohtani to return from IL Wednesday, but Dodgers still have unanswered questions in final week - Click here to listen to this article - The Dodgers have less than a week left of the regular season to round into playoff form. And their roster moves this series reflect that time crunch. Manager Dave Roberts confirmed Tuesday afternoon that Shohei Ohtani (right biceps, left knee) was on track to be reinstated from the 15-day injured list on Wednesday. Ohtani is feeling “considerably” be
item.content:encoded:
Shohei Ohtani to return from IL Wednesday, but Dodgers still have unanswered questions in final week
- Click here to listen to this article
-
The Dodgers have less than a week left of the regular season to round into playoff form. And their roster moves this series reflect that time crunch.
Manager Dave Roberts confirmed Tuesday afternoon that Shohei Ohtani (right biceps, left knee) was on track to be reinstated from the 15-day injured list on Wednesday. Ohtani is feeling “considerably” better than he was before the IL stint, according to Roberts.
“I would say if he was a five, he’s probably an eight or a nine right now,” Roberts said before eight pitchers led the Dodgers’ 7-0 win against the San Diego Padres.
On Tuesday, they returned two other important postseason pieces, reinstating center fielder Andy Pages (fractured left hand) and right-hander Roki Sasaki (right middle finger blister) from the injured list.
In corresponding moves, the Dodgers optioned right-hander Emmet Sheehan and catcher Eliézer Alfonzo to triple-A Oklahoma City.
Sasaki took the fourth inning of the bullpen game and threw scoreless ball. He gave up a pair of singles, but his fastball had a little extra life in the short stint, averaging 98.7 mph and topping out at 101.7.
Pages went 0 for 2 but reached base twice, on a hit by pitch and a walk.
Even as players return, however, there are still questions the Dodgers have to answer in the last week of the season:
Where will Ohtani hit?
At least at first, Roberts plans to write Ohtani in at the top of the order, per usual. But shortstop Mookie Betts has entered the conversation.
“Certainly versus right-handed pitching [Ohtani] will be there,” Roberts said. “I do think I should think through the Mookie versus left situation, but I have to think about the entire lineup structure.”
Ohtani has hit leadoff in every game he’s started this year. But he hit No. 2 in 79 games the two previous seasons combined.
Even without Ohtani, the Dodgers lineup has been clicking. On Tuesday, Tommy Edman hit his second home run in as many games, and Will Smith homered for the third time in four days.
Is the rotation healthy?
Dodgers left-hander Blake Snell, who exited his start last week with left groin tightness, threw a bullpen on Tuesday. He’s scheduled for one final regular-season start Saturday, Roberts said.
That means all four of the Dodgers’ projected playoff starters are lined up to pitch this Wednesday through Saturday, with Yoshinobu Yamamoto and Tyler Glasnow on the mound for the last two games against the Padres, and Tarik Skubal and Snell in the first two games in San Francisco.
Who is the closer?
In short, it could change by the day.
“In a perfect world, as we all know the world’s not perfect, I would love [a set closer],” Roberts said. “I think if there’s an opportunity, for example, for Tanner [Scott] to pitch a high-leverage inning in the seventh or the eighth inning, it’s just hard to pass that up if he’s the best option right there. Because you just don’t know where the ninth inning is going to be.
“Those are things that you have to kind of toil with, and those are always good things for people to debate. Right now I don’t see a one-person closer.”
Sasaki stepped into that role last year. It’s unclear exactly how Roberts will use him this time around, but Roberts said he could be an option, depending on how he pitches coming off the IL.
“Last year it was one of those things where it was a situation of need, as far as where we were at with performance and health and guys,” Roberts said. “He filled that role admirably.”
Who gets the last bench spot?
The battle to serve as the left-handed bat off the bench in the postseason has come down to rookie Josue De Paula and injured catcher Dalton Rushing (right flexor strain). But with Rushing still on the IL, De Paula appears to have an edge.
Don’t read too much into the Dodgers’ corresponding move for Ohtani on Wednesday. If they option De Paula 10 days out from the first game of the National League Division Series, he can still be included on the roster.
The Dodgers will have to make another roster move later in the week, when they plan to activate Rushing. If they option a player to make room for Rushing, that player would only be eligible for the start of the NLDS as the corresponding transaction for an IL move.

item.title: [MLB.com] Sasaki vuelve como relevista mientras Dodgers evalúan su bullpen para octubre
item.dc:creator: Sonja Chen
item.description: LOS ÁNGELES -- Roki Sasaki llamó la atención cuando pasó al bullpen durante la marcha del año pasado hacia el bicampeonato. Volverá a desempeñar ese papel en los últimos días de esta temporada regular y posiblemente vuelva a estar entre las opciones para cerrar juegos. Sasaki fue activado de la lista de lesionados de 15 días antes de la victoria por 7-0 sobre los Padres la noche del martes, como parte de una serie de movimientos que también incluyeron el regreso del cubano Andy Pagés de la lista
item.content:encoded:
LOS ÁNGELES -- Roki Sasaki llamó la atención cuando pasó al bullpen durante la marcha del año pasado hacia el bicampeonato. Volverá a desempeñar ese papel en los últimos días de esta temporada regular y posiblemente vuelva a estar entre las opciones para cerrar juegos.
Sasaki fue activado de la lista de lesionados de 15 días antes de la victoria por 7-0 sobre los Padres la noche del martes, como parte de una serie de movimientos que también incluyeron el regreso del cubano Andy Pagés de la lista de lesionados y el envío de Emmet Sheehan y el venezolano Eliezer Alfonzo a Triple-A Oklahoma City. Sasaki lanzó por última vez el 26 de agosto, cuando una ampolla en el dedo medio de la mano derecha puso fin prematuramente a su apertura contra los Bravos.
En su segunda temporada en Grandes Ligas, Sasaki se acercaba cada vez más a la versión de sí mismo que fue un fenómeno en la Liga Japonesa de Béisbol Profesional (NPB, por sus siglas en inglés). Tuvo marca de 5-5 con efectividad de 4.60 en 23 aperturas, pero esos números no cuentan toda la historia. Con un repertorio más amplio, que incluye un nuevo splitter, y una mayor velocidad en su recta, Sasaki tuvo su mejor tramo sostenido como abridor en Grandes Ligas, registrando efectividad de 2.63 en siete aperturas antes de lidiar con la ampolla.
“Emocionado de tener a Roki de vuelta”, dijo el manager Dave Roberts. “Está entusiasmado con este rol. Creo que puede tener un gran impacto, como lo tuvo el año pasado”.
En su regreso al bullpen el martes, Sasaki ponchó a dos en un cuarto inning en blanco, pese a permitir un par de sencillos con dos outs. Generó cuatro swings fallidos, incluidos dos en igual número de swings contra su splitter, y promedió 98.7 mph con las ocho rectas que lanzó, ligeramente por encima de su promedio de 97.8 mph esta temporada.
Los Dodgers mejoraron su récord a 97-60 después de que su juego de bullpen terminara en blanqueada. Están cinco juegos por delante de los Bravos en la lucha por el segundo mejor récord de la Liga Nacional y a uno de los Cerveceros, líderes del circuito y dueños del criterio de desempate entre ambos.
El año pasado, el traslado de Sasaki al relevo fue una decisión sin precedentes. Después de un comienzo por debajo de las expectativas en su temporada de novato y de perderse más de cuatro meses por una lesión en el hombro, la única oportunidad de Sasaki de contribuir con los Dodgers en la postemporada era pasar al bullpen.
Sasaki no sólo contribuyó, sino que se convirtió en el cerrador de los Dodgers en la postemporada, permitiendo apenas una carrera limpia en 10.2 innings, para efectividad de 0.84. La confianza que adquirió al conseguir resultados en Grandes Ligas, bajo la máxima presión, impulsó el regreso del derecho de 24 años a la rotación y su posterior despegue a mitad de esta temporada.
Actualmente, los Dodgers no cuentan con un cerrador fijo, ya que el boricua Edwin Díaz está lanzando en situaciones de baja presión en medio de sus dificultades a lo largo de la temporada, mientras busca ganarse un puesto en el bullpen para la postemporada. Díaz ponchó a dos en un quinto inning perfecto la noche del martes, su tercera presentación sin permitir carreras desde que regresó de la lista de lesionados.
Ha pasado mucho tiempo desde que Sasaki lanzó como relevista, pero si logra mostrarle lo suficiente a Roberts durante la última semana antes de la postemporada, podría convertirse en una opción para situaciones de salvamento.
“Creo que sin duda es una opción”, dijo Roberts. “Probablemente mucho dependerá de cómo lance esta noche. Seguramente tendrá una o dos presentaciones cortas más antes de que termine la temporada”.
Con Díaz perdiendo tiempo de juego por lesiones en el codo y el cuello, además de no lanzar bien cuando estuvo saludable, el zurdo Tanner Scott ha recibido la mayoría de las oportunidades de salvamento. Scott lidera a los Dodgers con 23 rescates, pero también ha desperdiciado cuatro oportunidades, incluidas dos desde comienzos de septiembre.
Scott todavía podría ser la mejor opción para cerrar los juegos, pero Sasaki podría complementarlo desde el lado derecho, algo importante debido a que el derecho venezolano Edgardo Henríquez estará fuera por el resto de la temporada regular debido a una distensión en la parte baja de la espalda. Se espera que regrese durante la postemporada.
Aunque a Roberts le gustaría contar con un cerrador en la postemporada, reconoció que es más probable que maneje el bullpen según los enfrentamientos. En esta época del año, algunas de las situaciones de mayor presión se presentan antes del noveno inning, por lo que tener varias opciones le permitiría utilizar a sus mejores relevistas en los momentos más convenientes.
“Creo que si hay una oportunidad, por ejemplo, de que Tanner lance un inning de alta presión en el séptimo u octavo, es difícil dejarla pasar si es la mejor opción en ese momento”, dijo Roberts. “Porque simplemente no sabes cómo se va a presentar el noveno inning”.

item.title: [New York Post] Dodgers shutout of Padres reveals potential (and unexpected) playoff strength
item.dc:creator: Jack Harris
item.description: Last year, the Dodgers hardly used their bullpen in the playoffs. This year, they would like that to once again be the blueprint. In their bid to three-peat as World Series champions, of course, the Dodgers are expected to be led by their star-studded rotation. Shohei Ohtani isn’t pitching, but Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Tarik Skubal, Blake Snell and Tyler Glasnow are. And if all goes according to plan, they will handle the bulk of the innings. item.content:encoded:
Last year, the Dodgers hardly used their bullpen in the playoffs.
This year, they would like that to once again be the blueprint.
In their bid to three-peat as World Series champions, of course, the Dodgers are expected to be led by their star-studded rotation. Shohei Ohtani isn’t pitching, but Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Tarik Skubal, Blake Snell and Tyler Glasnow are.
And if all goes according to plan, they will handle the bulk of the innings.
However, replicating the starting pitching excellence of last October won’t be easy. A season ago, the Dodgers’ four-man rotation of Ohtani, Yamamoto, Snell and Glasnow accounted for 113 of the team’s 165 postseason innings (including relief appearances from Glasnow and Yamamoto). Together, they posted a 2.55 ERA.
It was historic production.
Which also means, it’s fair to assume some regression will be possible –– both in workload and effectiveness.
Thus, having more reliable bullpen options this time around could be equally important for the Dodgers. And while that might have felt like a daunting reality earlier this year, when the unit was banged up and struggling through the middle portion of the campaign, Tuesday night was a reminder that the relief corps could be a strength in this fall’s title pursuit.
“Obviously we’ve had a lot of talent over the years,” manager Dave Roberts said. “But as far as sitting here today at the end of the season, it’s as good of shape as we’ve ever been in with the bullpen.”
In a 7-0 win over the San Diego Padres, the Dodgers were not supposed to have the pitching matchup –– countering Padres ace Michael King with a makeshift bullpen game in a rivalry series opener at Dodger Stadium.
Instead, eight different Dodgers relievers held the previous red-hot Padres to a five-hit shutout. Along the way, several arms who once seemed like question marks continued to round into increasingly promising form.
“It was fantastic,” Roberts said. “This is as good as our bullpen has been, has thrown.”
It started with opener Brock Stewart, a key right-handed weapon in the Dodgers’ bullpen who began the game with a scoreless first inning, continuing his late-season resurgence after another injury-plagued year.
From there, the baton was passed on down.
Justin Wrobleski, who is in the midst of a late-season conversion to the bullpen for the second-straight year, escaped a jam in the second. Blake Treinen, who might be on the postseason roster bubble given the Dodgers’ relief depth, offered one of his best outings of late by issuing only a two-out walk in a scoreless third.

California Post Sports Facebook, Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, X

California Post Newsletters: Sign up here!
California Post App: Download here!
Home delivery: Sign up here!
Page Six Hollywood: Sign up here!
The highlight of the night came in the fourth and fifth, when Roki Sasaki and Edwin Díaz hung a couple more zeroes in what were important appearances from each.
For Sasaki, the outing marked his first since returning from the injured list and making his own late-season move back to the bullpen, where he could reprise his role as closer from last year’s playoffs. He worked around a pair of singles with two strikeouts and a fastball that, even after being sidelined for the last month by a blister, sat at 99-100 mph.
For Díaz, Tuesday was not only a third-consecutive scoreless outing since his own return from the IL, but his most impressive yet as he makes a bid for the playoff roster. He retired the top of the Padres lineup in order with a pair of strikeouts, and has now retired 9 of 11 batters he has faced since rejoining the active roster.
Asked postgame if Díaz –– the $69 million offseason signing who lost the closer’s job amid a previously dismal debut Dodgers season –– could still pitch his way back into ninth-inning duties, Roberts said it’s “certainly possible.”
“The way he’s throwing, the ninth is possible, yes,” Roberts added.
By that point, the Dodgers had already pulled away from the Padres. They mounted a four-run rally with two outs in the second against King, who issued back-to-back bases-loaded walks to Tommy Edman and Mookie Betts before Freddie Freeman slashed a two-run single through the infield. The offense tacked on more runs in the fourth (on another Freeman RBI single), the sixth (on a solo home run from Tommy Edman), and the seventh (a Will Smith solo blast).
In what was the lineup’s toughest test in a while, they passed with flying colors.
Still, the night’s most encouraging developments came from the ‘pen, which capped off the game with two scoreless innings from Kyle Hurt, then stress-free appearances in the eighth and ninth from Alex Vesia and Jack Dreyer.
The unit’s most trusted arms at the moment, Tanner Scott (who figures to be vying with Sasaki for the postseason closer role) and Evan Phillips, weren’t even required. Nor was Edgardo Henriquez, who remains sidelined by a back injury but still could return in time for the playoffs.
“We know we have a good group, and anytime we get to carry the load and everybody has success and throws up zeros, it’s special,” Stewart said. “That’s really hard to do, for all eight guys or whatever it was today. So yeah, it’s cool.”
With a smirk, he added: “Write stories about it.”
Come October, of course, the Dodgers will be hoping their relievers are the main story.
But if the rotation falters, the club seems significantly better-suited to handle it than it did a year ago.
“That could change in a day, in a game, as we all know,” Roberts said. “But right now, feel really good about everyone out there.”

item.title: [DodgersBeat] Dalton Rushing Faces Dodgers Postseason Roster Battle
item.dc:creator: Los Royers
item.description: LOS ANGELES, CA — Dalton Rushing may have only three regular-season games to convince the Los Angeles Dodgers that he should be their left-handed bat off the bench in October. Manager Dave Roberts acknowledged Tuesday that Rushing’s missed time creates a difficult path as the Dodgers compare him with top prospect Josue De Paula for a potential postseason bench role. De Paula’s recent run of consistent at-bats gives him an important advantage entering the final week. “It’s going to be tougher for
item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES, CA — Dalton Rushing may have only three regular-season games to convince the Los Angeles Dodgers that he should be their left-handed bat off the bench in October.
Manager Dave Roberts acknowledged Tuesday that Rushing’s missed time creates a difficult path as the Dodgers compare him with top prospect Josue De Paula for a potential postseason bench role. De Paula’s recent run of consistent at-bats gives him an important advantage entering the final week.
“It’s going to be tougher for Dalton, given the time that he’s missed,” Roberts said. “To think that you have three games to get back into playoff form—which is tough to do.”
Rushing has resumed taking at-bats as he works back from the right elbow discomfort that sent him to the injured list earlier this month. Roberts said the Dodgers hope to activate him at some point during the final series of the regular season, giving the club a brief opportunity to evaluate how he looks as a pinch-hitting option.
What the Dodgers will evaluate
The Dodgers are looking beyond raw results as they decide which left-handed hitter gives them the better postseason option. Roberts said the evaluation will focus on the quality and structure of each plate appearance.
“Quality of at-bat, conducting an at-bat, obviously the ability to swing at strikes, take balls, get on base, get a hit,” Roberts said. “There’s potential slug with both those guys.”
Producing off the bench presents a different challenge from playing every day. A postseason reserve might receive one plate appearance against a premium reliever and be expected to control the strike zone without the benefit of several earlier at-bats.
That makes recent game action especially important. De Paula has remained active since making the jump from Double-A to the Dodgers, while Rushing must attempt to recover his timing immediately after another interruption to his season.
“It’s not, again, a knock on him,” Roberts said of Rushing. “He’s been great for us, but it’s still tough, right, given also where you’re talking about having the consistency of at-bats recently from Josue.”
No postseason roster decision yet
Roberts did not declare De Paula the winner of the roster competition. He called the comparison “a good debate” and said the Dodgers still need to discuss which hitter gives them the best chance in a limited bench role.
Rushing’s immediate path is expected to come as a hitter rather than a catcher. If he is activated for the final three games, every plate appearance could carry added weight as the Dodgers finalize their postseason roster.
De Paula has already impressed the organization during his first major-league opportunity. Rushing, however, offers his own combination of strike-zone control and power. The final decision could come down to whether three games provide enough evidence that his timing has returned.

The Dodgers activated right-hander Roki Sasaki and center fielder Andy Pages off the IL on Tuesday, a major development in the lead
item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES -- Shohei Ohtani is expected to return to the lineup Wednesday, the first day he is eligible to be activated off the injured list, and Los Angeles Dodgers manager Dave Roberts says he looks "considerably" healthier than he did a couple of weeks ago.
"If he was a five, he's probably an eight or a nine right now," Roberts said, referencing a 1-to-10 scale.
The Dodgers activated right-hander Roki Sasaki and center fielder Andy Pages off the IL on Tuesday, a major development in the leadup to October.
Sasaki, who has been recovering from a blister suffered in an Aug. 26 start, was available out of the bullpen for Tuesday's series opener against the San Diego Padres and could be an option to again close out games in the postseason. Pages, who fractured his left hand on Aug. 22, will reprise his role as an everyday player at a premium position.
Ohtani landed on the IL because of lingering pain in his right biceps and left knee on Sept. 8 but began a hitting progression seven days ago and advanced to taking as many as 40 swings off Trajekt, the popular pitching simulator, on Saturday. Ohtani also ran the bases that day. On Tuesday, he went through his typical pregame workout.
Ohtani, 32, will only hit the rest of this season and was struggling in that realm before landing on the IL, compiling only seven hits and 22 strikeouts over his past 54 at-bats. Roberts previously indicated the plan was for Ohtani to play in all of the Dodgers' remaining five regular-season games to get reacclimated to major league pitching.
Where he hits, though, is up for debate. In all likelihood, Ohtani will continue to lead off against opposing right-handed pitchers. But Mookie Betts' recent hot streak -- heading into this week, he was hitting.373/.468/.746 in September -- has Roberts weighing the possibility of batting him leadoff against lefties.
What Ohtani's return means for outfield prospect Josue De Paula is also an open question.
De Paula, 21, has eight hits and 10 walks in 38 plate appearances since temporarily replacing Ohtani at designated hitter. The Dodgers are strongly considering him as an option to be a left-handed bat off the bench during the postseason, though they might send him down as the corresponding move for activating Ohtani to give him at-bats in this week's Triple-A championship series.
The other candidate would be backup catcher Dalton Rushing, who has an elbow injury that is preventing him from throwing. Rushing is expected to be activated at some point in the next three days, but Roberts acknowledged it would be difficult for him to be thrust into a pinch-hitting role in October after playing in only four games since the start of September.
"There's potential slug with both those guys," Roberts said. "It's going to be a good debate."

Manager Dave Roberts said Snell is in line to start on Saturday in San Fr
item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES — It’s the final week of the regular season and the Dodgers are sorting things out as they prepare for the postseason, which they hope will start on October 3 in the National League Division Series rather than September 29 in the wild card round.
Before Tuesday’s game, Blake Snell pitched a bullpen session at Dodger Stadium as he works his way back from leaving last Wednesday’s start with left groin discomfort. Manager Dave Roberts said Snell is in line to start on Saturday in San Francisco against the Giants, with Tarik Skubal — currently on the bereavement list — starting Friday night at Oracle Park.
Yoshinobu Yamamoto starts Wednesday and Tyler Glasnow Thursday against the Padres.
Also on Tuesday, reliever Will Klein pitched a simulated inning against Dalton Rushing in a battle of players on the injured list. Klein is on the 60-day injured list with elbow discomfort and not eligible to be activated until September 30 at the earliest, but it looks like he’ll be in the stay-hot camp should the Dodgers have room to add him at some point later in the postseason, similar to in 2025 when Klein wasn’t active until the World Series and he pitched five scoreless innings, including four innings in the marathon Game 3.
“With Will it’s more get healthy, show that you’re healthy, throw to some hitters,” Roberts said. “He’ll throw during the week off, then we’ll kind of see if there’s an opportunity later on in the postseason, sort of like last year.”
Rushing is trying to work his way back from elbow discomfort suffered when practicing throwing. His role would be a left-handed bat off the bench, a role currently occupied by Josue De Paula, who has been the designated hitter with Shohei Ohtani out. But Ohtani is expected to be activated Wednesday barring an unforeseen setback.
That essentially sets up a battle between Rushing and De Paula for a postseason roster spot, though Roberts said the plan is to activate Rushing at some point this week to literally get back into the swing of things.
“Quality of at-bat, conducting an at-bat obviously, the ability to swing at strikes, take balls, get on base, get a hit. There’s potential slug with both guys. I think it’s a good debate,” Roberts said. “Hitting off the bench is very difficult so we’re trying to figure out who gives us the best chance.
“And to be quite frank, it’s going to be tougher for Dalton given the time he’s missed, and to think that you have [three] games to get back into playoff form, it’s tough to do. It’s not a knock on him, he’s been great for us, but it’s still tough, right, Given that we talk about having the consistency of at-bats recently from Josue. But we have to have those conversations and make a decision.”
Activating both Ohtani and Rushing this week, when the Dodgers have 14 active position players, would require two corresponding moves to make room on the active roster. If De Paula doesn’t get sent down — “I think Josue has done a fantastic job,” Roberts said Tuesday — that might mean rough news for Alexes Call and Freeland, either this week or next.

item.content:encoded:
LOS ÁNGELES (AP) — Se espera que Shohei Ohtani vuelva a la alineación de los Dodgers de Los Ángeles el miércoles tras una etapa en la lista de lesionados.
La superestrella ha estado en la lista de lesionados desde el 9 de septiembre debido a una inflamación en el bíceps derecho y a un dolor persistente en la rodilla izquierda.
El mánager Dave Roberts comentó que Ohtani se siente “considerablemente” mejor.
“Yo diría que si estaba en un cinco, ahora probablemente está en un ocho o un nueve”, manifestó Roberts el martes antes de que los Dodgers enfrentaran a San Diego.
Los Dodgers aseguraron su 13er título del Oeste de la Liga Nacional en 14 años sin Ohtani, quien estaba en Los Ángeles recibiendo tratamiento cuando el equipo venció a Cincinnati como visitante la semana pasada. Ahora, el cuatro veces MVP tendrá cinco juegos restantes para tomar algunos turnos al bate antes de que comience la postemporada.
Es probable que Ohtani retome su papel como primer bate de los Dodgers, especialmente contra lanzadores derechos. Mookie Betts ha estado encabezando la alineación y batea para .373 este mes.
“Probablemente así es como va a quedar, pero todavía no lo he decidido del todo”, señaló Roberts, y añadió que consideraría el valor de Betts como primer bate contra lanzadores zurdos. “Tengo que pensar en toda la estructura de la alineación”.
___

item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers have been without superstar slugger Shohei Ohtani for the last week+ as he's been dealing with a biceps issue that led to his IL placement.
Manager Dave Roberts indicated on Tuesday, before the Dodgers' series opener with the San Diego Padres, that Ohtani will be activated from the IL on Wednesday.
However, in Ohtani's absence, the Dodgers have implemented infielder Mookie Betts in the leadoff spot, and Mookie has been on fire at the plate, which leaves Roberts at a crossroads.
More MLB on Heavy: Los Angeles Dodgers Dealt Good Blake Snell News Before Padres Game
Dave Roberts Reveals Tough Decision Ahead with Leadoff Batter
Dave Roberts indicated to the media on Tuesday evening that he isn't entirely sure who will lead off between Mookie Betts and Shohei Ohtani when Ohtani returns from the IL.
"Dave Roberts said he is still debating who will lead off when Ohtani returns, but said it will most likely be dependent upon pitching matchups So, Ohtani vs RHP and Mookie Betts vs LHP"
It might be wise for the Dodgers to get Shohei Ohtani in a different role, as he's been slumping over the past month+.
As for Mookie Betts, he's starting to hit an offensive stride after struggling for most of the season.
It will be very interesting to see how Roberts handles Mookie Betts and Shohei Ohtani's lineup spots in the last week of the regular season.
Dodgers reporter Bill Plunkett wrote (about the situation):
"Dave Roberts said "as of now" Shohei Ohtani will return to the leadoff spot when he comes off IL Wednesday but it's something he is giving further thought to. Could be a case where Ohtani hits first v RH Betts v LH"
